a89.speaker: Ulf Laessing, regional expert
a89.name: Ulf Laessing
a89.title: regional expert
a89.speech: Notes that Washington has already offered to eliminate certain extremist leaders on condition of obtaining access to the exploitation of natural resources.

a89.speaker: Troy Fitrell, US official
a89.name: Troy Fitrell
a89.title: US official
a89.speech: Declared, in Abidjan in May, that trade, and not aid, would be the pillar of the new American policy in Africa.

a89.speaker: Dorothy Shea, US official
a89.name: Dorothy Shea
a89.title: US official
a89.speech: Underscores at the UN that the destabilization of the region could directly affect American interests.

a131.speaker: Burmese ruling junta
a131.name: Burmese ruling junta
a131.speech: Said that at least 1,644 people were killed and 3,408 injured, mostly in the Mandalay region, considered the worst hit.

a131.speaker: Red Cross official (unnamed)
a131.name: Red Cross official (unnamed)
a131.speech: According to a Red Cross official, more than 90 people are reportedly trapped in the rubble of a twelve-storey residential building in Mandalay.

a131.speaker: Soldier stationed at a checkpoint outside the collapsed temple (unnamed)
a131.name: Soldier stationed at a checkpoint outside the collapsed temple (unnamed)
a131.speech: Testified: “A monk died. There are also injured people, we pulled them out of the rubble and they were taken to hospital.”

a131.speaker: Teacher trapped in the rubble of a private secondary school (unnamed), reported by rescuers
a131.name: Teacher trapped in the rubble of a private secondary school (unnamed)
a131.title: reported by rescuers
a131.speech: Reportedly cried out: “I am alive inside. Help me, please, I am thirsty.”

a131.speaker: Residents of the Mandalay suburb
a131.name: Residents of the Mandalay suburb
a131.speech: Said at least seven people were still trapped inside on Saturday, including two teachers and several children, and that seven other people died.

a131.speaker: Security officer at Mandalay airport (unnamed)
a131.name: Security officer at Mandalay airport (unnamed)
a131.speech: Said: “It has been closed since yesterday” (Friday). “The ceiling collapsed but nobody was injured.”

a131.speaker: Min Aung Hlaing, head of the Burmese junta
a131.name: Min Aung Hlaing
a131.title: head of the Burmese junta
a131.speech: Made a rare appeal for international aid, inviting “any country, any organisation” to provide assistance.

a131.speaker: Burmese authorities
a131.name: Burmese authorities
a131.speech: Declared a state of emergency in the six most affected regions.

a131.speaker: China
a131.name: China
a131.speech: Said it had sent 82 rescuers, and pledged to provide 13.8 million dollars in emergency humanitarian aid.

a131.speaker: United Nations
a131.name: United Nations
a131.speech: Warned on Saturday that a “serious shortage” of medical supplies is affecting the assistance deployed on the ground, stressing that rescuers were lacking in particular “trauma kits”, blood bags, anaesthetic products and certain essential medicines.

a131.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a131.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a131.speech: Said it had urgently sent nearly 3 tonnes of medical supplies to the hospitals of Mandalay and Naypyidaw where thousands of injured people are being treated.

a131.speaker: Marie Manrique, Red Cross official in Burma
a131.name: Marie Manrique
a131.title: Red Cross official in Burma
a131.speech: Stressed: “We have a few encouraging accounts of people being found, but the sad stories will keep coming” ; observed that it is necessary to “start thinking about what is going to happen” to the disaster victims who have lost their housing in the catastrophe.

a131.speaker: Humanitarian agencies
a131.name: Humanitarian agencies
a131.speech: Warned that Burma was absolutely not prepared to face such a tragedy, at a time when some 3.5 million people have been displaced because of the ongoing conflict.

a131.speaker: United Nations
a131.name: United Nations
a131.speech: According to the UN, famine, even before the earthquake, was already threatening 15 million people this year across the country.

a131.speaker: People’s Defence Forces (PDF), Burmese rebels
a131.name: People’s Defence Forces (PDF)
a131.title: Burmese rebels
a131.speech: Decreed a partial two-week ceasefire starting Sunday in order to facilitate rescue operations; said the group will not attack the army – but will defend itself if necessary – and assured that it would “collaborate with the UN and NGOs to ensure the security, transport and establishment of temporary relief and medical camps” in the areas it controls.

a131.speaker: Chadchart Sittipunt, Governor of Bangkok
a131.name: Chadchart Sittipunt
a131.title: Governor of Bangkok
a131.speech: Told AFP that at least eight people died at the collapsed construction site and eight others were rescued alive there, but 79 people were still missing ; said about 400 people spent the night from Friday to Saturday in open parks because of the emergency, their homes not being safe enough to return to.

a131.speaker: Thai authorities
a131.name: Thai authorities
a131.speech: Said thermal imaging drones detected signs of life of at least 30 people in the rubble.

a131.speaker: Spokesperson (unnamed)
a131.name: Spokesperson (unnamed)
a131.speech: Told AFP that a woman had to give birth in the open air after being evacuated from a hospital and that a surgeon continued to operate on a patient outside, after it was necessary to leave the operating theatre urgently.

a323.speaker: Councillor of the Tobias Hainyeko Constituency
a323.name: Councillor of the Tobias Hainyeko Constituency
a323.speech: Says violence affects not only women, who face the brunt of physical and emotional abuse, but also men and children, who may witness or experience trauma.

a323.speaker: Local stakeholders including the Walvis Bay Corridor Group, the Voluntary Medical Male Circumcision Initiative, Project Hope Initiatives and the Ministry of Health and Social Services
a323.name: Local stakeholders including the Walvis Bay Corridor Group
a323.title: the Voluntary Medical Male Circumcision Initiative, Project Hope Initiatives and the Ministry of Health and Social Services
a323.speech: Highlighted the services available to support victims of gender-based violence and encouraged residents to seek help and not succumb to it.

a356.speaker: Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of the World Health Organization (WHO)
a356.name: Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a356.title: Director-General of the World Health Organization (WHO)
a356.speech: Warned that the funding cuts imposed by the Trump administration could lead to a "catastrophic" disruption in the supply of antiretroviral drugs in several African countries.

a356.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a356.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a356.speech: According to WHO, Somaliland is among the areas at risk.

a356.speaker: Dr. Mustafe Abdillahi Hussein, physician at the Tuberculosis Hospital in Hargeisa
a356.name: Dr. Mustafe Abdillahi Hussein
a356.title: physician at the Tuberculosis Hospital in Hargeisa
a356.speech: Told BBC Somali that the potential aid gap threatens to undo years of progress in treating HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis.

a356.speaker: Somaliland HIV/AIDS Commission
a356.name: Somaliland HIV/AIDS Commission
a356.speech: According to the Commission, 2,092 patients across the region receive monthly antiretroviral medication funded by the Global Fund, a health financing body heavily supported by the United States.

a356.speaker: Aamina, a woman living with HIV
a356.name: Aamina
a356.title: a woman living with HIV
a356.speech: Told the BBC that her local clinic recently warned of dwindling drug supplies: "I've always collected my medication from the HIV/AIDS outpatient ward at the General Hospital. But they told us the funding has decreased, and since last month, we haven't received our medication as reliably." ; "If these medications stop, our immune systems weaken. Illnesses come back. We suffer, and eventually, we die."

a356.speaker: Hussein Bashir Hirsi, Somaliland Health Minister
a356.name: Hussein Bashir Hirsi
a356.title: Somaliland Health Minister
a356.speech: Acknowledged that the aid cuts would have an impact but insisted the government has made contingency plans: "Yes, this will affect us. But it does not mean patients will be left without medication. We are prepared. If the support ends, we will procure the drugs ourselves."

a410.speaker: Abidine Ould Sidewa, nurse at Mbera refugee camp triage centre, Mauritania
a410.name: Abidine Ould Sidewa
a410.title: nurse at Mbera refugee camp triage centre, Mauritania
a410.speech: On what led him to humanitarian work: “I started as a trader in Timbuktu (in Mali), but it was when I discovered community health work that I truly understood what it meant, such as being helpful, listening and supporting others. This is what inspired me to train as a nurse in 1998. Since then, I have been committed to serving all people in need, regardless of their origin. Since April 2024, I have been working at the triage centre for new arrivals from Mali. We provide consultations, malnutrition screening, vaccinations for zero-dose children and awareness-raising. This system enables us to identify individuals who are ill before they integrate into the community, which has significantly reduced community deaths.”

a410.speaker: Abidine Ould Sidewa, nurse at Mbera refugee camp triage centre, Mauritania
a410.name: Abidine Ould Sidewa
a410.title: nurse at Mbera refugee camp triage centre, Mauritania
a410.speech: On common diseases and awareness-raising: “In the field, I deal with diseases that mainly affect children and women: Acute respiratory infections, malaria, diarrhoea diseases, measles and mostly, malnutrition. These conditions are often worsened by a lack of access to healthcare, safe drinking water and a balanced diet. To raise awareness among the population, I take a tailored approach for each context. I talk to mothers, community leaders and young people. I inform them about the importance of vaccination, simple hygiene practices, the risks associated with births unattended by a skilled health worker and the benefits of exclusive breastfeeding. I also rely on community leaders and dialogue sessions to convey messages clearly and respectfully. I always emphasise the importance of following vaccination schedule, as it saves lives.”

a410.speaker: Abidine Ould Sidewa, nurse at Mbera refugee camp triage centre, Mauritania
a410.name: Abidine Ould Sidewa
a410.title: nurse at Mbera refugee camp triage centre, Mauritania
a410.speech: On a memorable incident: “In 2022, I met a pregnant refugee woman, alone with two young children, both suffering from severe malnutrition. She was distrustful, exhausted and refused treatment for religious reasons. I took the time to listen to her, to understand her fears and beliefs. It wasn't easy, but little by little, she began to trust me. I arranged for her to be transferred to a health centre, organised nutritional care for her children and accompanied her throughout her journey, right up to delivery. She gave birth to a healthy baby. That day, she thanked me emotionally. It brought tears to my eyes.”

a410.speaker: Abidine Ould Sidewa, nurse at Mbera refugee camp triage centre, Mauritania
a410.name: Abidine Ould Sidewa
a410.title: nurse at Mbera refugee camp triage centre, Mauritania
a410.speech: On the future of local humanitarian action: “I see real transformation: Communities are becoming aware of their role, asking questions and getting involved. Collaboration with the police, the structured reception of new arrivals and growing interest in health show that humanitarian work is no longer limited to emergencies. It is becoming a driver of recovery and empowerment. For me, reaching the most vulnerable is not just about providing care or resources. Above all, it means recognising their humanity and their fundamental right to live in safety, in good health and with hope. Humanitarian aid begins when we refuse to look away. By strengthening the capacity of local communities to care for themselves, we are not only saving lives: We are planting the seeds of a more equitable, dignified and united future.”

a473.speaker: Edvaldo Cardoso, Boavista da Praia (national champions)
a473.name: Edvaldo Cardoso
a473.title: Boavista da Praia (national champions)
a473.speech: On revalidating the national title for the Cape Verde Championship, said that the objective also involves revalidating the title: “We have five national champion titles and we are going to try to be back-to-back champions”, noting that this wish will not be easy because Boavista is now “a target to be shot down”.

a473.speaker: Cape Verdean Football Federation (FCF)
a473.name: Cape Verdean Football Federation (FCF)
a473.speech: Announced that the final of the National Championship will be played in São Vicente and that the “Final Four” of the Cape Verde Cup will have the island of Santo Antão as its stage.

a481.speaker: Saad Hariri, leader of the Sunni Future Movement
a481.name: Saad Hariri
a481.title: leader of the Sunni Future Movement
a481.speech: Accuses Syria of being behind the February 2005 assassination of his father, former Prime Minister Rafic Hariri.

a481.speaker: International Crisis Group, May 2013 report "Too Close for Comfort: Syrians in Lebanon"
a481.name: International Crisis Group
a481.title: May 2013 report "Too Close for Comfort: Syrians in Lebanon"
a481.speech: Laid out that the presence of Syrian refugees is exacerbating existing political, social and communal tensions and exposing Lebanon's own dysfunction.

a481.speaker: International Crisis Group, May 2014 report "Lebanon's Hizbollah Turns Eastward to Syria"
a481.name: International Crisis Group
a481.title: May 2014 report "Lebanon's Hizbollah Turns Eastward to Syria"
a481.speech: Argued that Lebanese society is deeply polarised over Hizbollah's military involvement in Syria.

a481.speaker: Hizbollah leader (unnamed)
a481.name: Hizbollah leader (unnamed)
a481.speech: Openly criticising the Saudi royal family and its military operations in Yemen.

a481.speaker: Some Lebanese Sunni voices
a481.name: Some Lebanese Sunni voices
a481.speech: Now believe that Hizbollah's fight inside Syria prevents the "black threat", named for the colour of the Islamic State's flag, from penetrating into Lebanon.

a613.speaker: Hunger Hotspots report (joint FAO-WFP early warning report)
a613.name: Hunger Hotspots report (joint FAO-WFP early warning report)
a613.speech: Warns that people in five hunger hotspots around the world face extreme hunger and risk of starvation and death in the coming months unless there is urgent humanitarian action and a coordinated international effort to de-escalate conflict, stem displacement, and mount an urgent full-scale aid response ; shows that Sudan, Palestine, South Sudan, Haiti and Mali are hotspots of highest concern, with communities already facing famine, at risk of famine or confronted with catastrophic levels of acute food insecurity due to intensifying or persisting conflict, economic shocks, and natural hazards ; projects a serious deterioration of acute food insecurity in 13 countries and territories, with Yemen, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Myanmar and Nigeria now hotspots of very high concern, and other hotspots including Burkina Faso, Chad, Somalia, and Syria ; highlights the importance of continued investments in early humanitarian action.

a613.speaker: QU Dongyu, FAO Director-General
a613.name: QU Dongyu
a613.title: FAO Director-General
a613.speech: "This report makes it very clear: hunger today is not a distant threat - it is a daily emergency for millions." ; "We must act now, and act together, to save lives and safeguard livelihoods. Protecting people's farms and animals to ensure they can keep producing food where they are, even in the toughest and harshest conditions, is not just urgent - it is essential."

a613.speaker: Cindy McCain, World Food Programme Executive Director
a613.name: Cindy McCain
a613.title: World Food Programme Executive Director
a613.speech: "This report is a red alert. We know where hunger is rising and we know who is at risk." ; "We have the tools and experience to respond, but without funding and access, we cannot save lives. Urgent, sustained investment in food assistance and recovery support is crucial as the window to avert yet more devastating hunger is closing fast."

a613.speaker: IPC (Integrated Food Security Phase Classification) update on South Sudan
a613.name: IPC (Integrated Food Security Phase Classification) update on South Sudan
a613.speech: An IPC update released after the report's finalization indicated Risk of Famine in two areas of the country and confirmed the bleak outlook.

a613.speaker: FAO and WFP
a613.name: FAO and WFP
a613.speech: Warn that gains in Ethiopia, Kenya, Lebanon, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger, Zambia and Zimbabwe, which have been removed from the Hunger Hotspots list, remain fragile and could reverse quickly if shocks re-emerge.

a613.speaker: Government of Sudan
a613.name: Government of Sudan
a613.speech: Did not endorse the December 2024 IPC analysis.

a615.speaker: Government of Zambia
a615.name: Government of Zambia
a615.speech: Has announced that Zambia will be engaging officials from the United States government to address the suspension of HIV drug distribution to developing countries.

a615.speaker: Dr George Sinyangwe, Ministry of Health's Permanent Secretary for Donor Coordination
a615.name: Dr George Sinyangwe
a615.title: Ministry of Health's Permanent Secretary for Donor Coordination
a615.speech: Says following the announcement by President Donald Trump to suspend aid, Zambia would soon be engaging the USA government for talks over the matter ; said government would release an official position today.

a621.speaker: Major General Mahamadou Ibrahim Bagadoma, Governor of the Diffa Region
a621.name: Major General Mahamadou Ibrahim Bagadoma
a621.title: Governor of the Diffa Region
a621.speech: In his address, recalled the scale of malaria in Niger, particularly in the Diffa region, where the disease remains one of the leading causes of illness and death: "Malaria is a major public health problem in Niger and ranks first in terms of cause of morbidity and mortality. In 2024, the Diffa region recorded 90,650 confirmed cases with 172 deaths, against 77,381 cases and 94 deaths between January and September 2025." ; stressed that this situation has serious health and socio-economic repercussions, affecting above all vulnerable groups such as children, pregnant women, people with disabilities, as well as displaced and refugee populations.

a621.speaker: Major General Mahamadou Ibrahim Bagadoma, Governor of the Diffa Region
a621.name: Major General Mahamadou Ibrahim Bagadoma
a621.title: Governor of the Diffa Region
a621.speech: Regarding collective protection, insisted on the importance of dusting insecticides along the main thoroughfares, sanitation of living environments (disposal of waste water, drainage of rainwater), as well as on community awareness-raising and the seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC) campaign.

a621.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a621.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a621.speech: According to the WHO, malaria is an acute febrile parasitic disease, potentially fatal, transmitted to humans by the bite of infected female anopheles mosquitoes; although curable and preventable, it can lead to serious complications and even death if not treated quickly.

a843.speaker: Gizachew Sisay, UNDP (innovative finance lab)
a843.name: Gizachew Sisay
a843.title: UNDP (innovative finance lab)
a843.speech: "The innovative finance lab initiated by the UNDP in collaboration with the National Bank of Ethiopia. They realised that the micro-small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) have been underserved or have less access to finance. Studies found that most are missing the middle because they are too big for microfinance institutions and too small for banks. The innovative finance lab stepped in to identify, explore, test and experiment the alternative financial instruments that can work for the MSMEs in Ethiopia."

a843.speaker: Ali Zafar
a843.name: Ali Zafar
a843.speech: "Innovative finance lab comes with experience from other parts of the world, especially from East Asia. Some firms were historically absent from the banking sector, and various instruments and mechanisms. These small and medium firms will get the finance to scale up and reach a specific size. No country has developed without a vibrant and well-developed financial sector. The innovative finance lab is a pioneer of this new effort to bring finance to firms that have not made it part of the financial ecosystem."

a843.speaker: Ali Zafar
a843.name: Ali Zafar
a843.speech: On targeting the "missing middle": "There are many innovative firms in Ethiopia without being able to get funds from the banking sector. This is because; either they do not have the history or a broad network. It is an excellent opportunity to graduate the firms, scale up, solve the binding constraints and finance them. The lab is not established to partner with big and established firms but to go after firms of a specific capability that have the potential to scale up." ; "We are not targeting the established players in the industry who have access to the banking sector. The ICT sector has a lot of new innovative startups that are emerging. We are looking at firms with sufficient scale and vision without being established."

a843.speaker: Gizachew Sisay, UNDP
a843.name: Gizachew Sisay
a843.title: UNDP
a843.speech: On the lab's phases and longevity: "We have three phases. We will take a lead role as UNDP and drive it together with the National Bank of Ethiopia using the setup mechanism. The second phase tests the scale of whether the alternative financial instruments will work. The lab will stay there. Its shape and scope might change over time. In the final phase, the lab will be there, but gradually it will be taken by the government to be a financial modality that can work for MSMEs, and our role will gradually diminish."

a843.speaker: Gizachew Sisay, UNDP
a843.name: Gizachew Sisay
a843.title: UNDP
a843.speech: On selection of enterprises: "The lab will be working with the Ministry of Technology, looking for micro startups with innovative ideas, but cannot commercialise them due to a lack of finance. The Technical Assistance Facility (TAF) will be doing this. It will do the due diligence and select the micro, small or medium enterprises based on their growth potential. It refers the enterprises to the Enterprise Financing Facility (EFF), another segment of the finance lab. This year, we aim to reach out to 100 MSMEs." ; "The Technical Assistance Facility will do the technical clearance. It will have a due diligence process, and anyone eligible will access the funds. The advisory board will decide on the overall envelope size and how the lab should operate."

a843.speaker: Gizachew Sisay, UNDP
a843.name: Gizachew Sisay
a843.title: UNDP
a843.speech: On the launch and governance structure: "The innovative and finance lab board will be elected and conduct its first meeting to endorse the terms of reference for the board. The board will also endorse and disclose development partners who will be informed of the purpose of the lab. The governance system will get a green light. The board will have an advisory role and provide strategic guidance. Both the UNDP and the National Bank of Ethiopia serve as secretariat. The lab is structured to have a separate office and experts doing the day-to-day activities." ; "The board is a mixture of government and private sector members, including the UN. Ministries of Finance, Labour & Job Creation, as well as Innovation & Technology, will be represented by their state ministers. Financial institutions and private sector representatives will take part."

a843.speaker: Ali Zafar
a843.name: Ali Zafar
a843.speech: On board selection: "They are selected based on technical competence and excellence. The lab's vision is to have the public and private sectors together on the board." ; "The board is not a classic bureaucratic board, but a mix of public and private operators who bring in the same equation to have a conversation and exercise due diligence. I think this is innovative about this project."

a843.speaker: Gizachew Sisay, UNDP
a843.name: Gizachew Sisay
a843.title: UNDP
a843.speech: On funding: "By making it work for its purpose. If it can work as planned, we assume everyone will jump on it - venture capitalists, crowdfunding, or alternative mechanism we use to make it work. We are taking the lead; the UNDP management is committed to financing the lab with one million dollars to set it up. We have already deployed the technical assistance facility for nearly half a million dollars. We are committed to investing from the technical assistance facility; but for the enterprise financing facility, it should come from other sources, including banks in Ethiopia." ; "In the first phase, the lab aims to set up a finance facility of 10 million dollars that will gradually reach the second phase of 100 million." ; On Dashen Bank being onboard: "Yes. Others will also come in the future."

a843.speaker: Ali Zafar
a843.name: Ali Zafar
a843.speech: On the financing model: "The sustainability and financing model will not be for all brands. It will be a model of various financial instruments, including subsidised credits. We cannot tell you exactly how big it will be in five years. We need to understand the market more and see which players will come to the demonstration effect. But the financing model will be a combination of initially UNDP, some donors and then refunds of the money."

a843.speaker: Ali Zafar
a843.name: Ali Zafar
a843.speech: On job creation: "We cannot give exact numbers, but we are optimistic that the employment gains from these MSMEs can be pretty significant. Our data is a lot from East Asia, even from places like India, where you have seen Fintech startups; startups in the manufacturing space catalysed very quickly within years. We hope there is a demonstration and a catalytic effect. Once you have some emerging firms, other firms see those firms and want to join. It is like a snowball effect."

a843.speaker: Ali Zafar
a843.name: Ali Zafar
a843.speech: On targeted sectors and GDP: "Yes, but economics is not static; it is dynamic. Look at the GDP composition in China or Vietnam in the 1980s, and contrast it between 2000 and 2010. By helping scale up different sectors and firms, the innovative lab can create more windows within sectors and eventually have a catalytic role. Most countries in the world began somewhere. We want to identify the next promising firms in Ethiopia in these sectors. There is tremendous potential in the Ethiopian economy, and we believe that we want to tap into that potential and then open up the space."

a843.speaker: Gizachew Sisay, UNDP
a843.name: Gizachew Sisay
a843.title: UNDP
a843.speech: On regulatory and policy reform: "We have been exploring the policy document of the National Bank, and banks are expected to dedicate five percent of their resources to MSMEs. None of them is implementing this. That is the one policy agenda that we are promoting. Small businesses should have a service window because they are a nurturing ground for big companies."

a843.speaker: Ali Zafar
a843.name: Ali Zafar
a843.speech: On forex and governance: "The innovative finance lab will address the forex problem. We envision an excellent governance framework, which is why we also have extensive experience and hybrid managers."

a843.speaker: Ali Zafar
a843.name: Ali Zafar
a843.speech: On the macroeconomic crisis: "The country has experienced several shocks in the last four to five years, beginning with a pandemic, drought, the northern Ethiopia war and the Ukraine war. It is true that there have been macroeconomic challenges. But a crisis is also an opportunity. Great reforms have been done during periods of crisis. India reformed in the 1990s. We think it is the right time to reform the financial sector to overcome some of the after-shocks coming from the outside. A more robust and resilient Ethiopian economy is needed in a world of global strength."

a843.speaker: Gizachew Sisay, UNDP
a843.name: Gizachew Sisay
a843.title: UNDP
a843.speech: On hope for the Ethiopian economy: "We see the potential and the opportunity for the Ethiopian economy to grow for we have a very dynamic youth population."

a843.speaker: Ali Zafar
a843.name: Ali Zafar
a843.speech: On donor cuts and resource mobilisation: "Aid worldwide is in decline. The Ukraine war has separated many essential points. However, many donors are interested in this innovative financial space. In this ecosystem of supporting startups, there is a lot of consensus of interest."

a843.speaker: Tamrat G. Giorgis, Managing Editor of Addis Fortune (interviewer)
a843.name: Tamrat G. Giorgis
a843.title: Managing Editor of Addis Fortune (interviewer)
a843.speech: Put it to the interviewees that asset-based loan guarantees and securing concessional loans for businesses not served by the traditional banking system is not a new concept, noting that the UK DiFD, the USAID and MasterCard Foundation have been doing it for years, and asked what else they were planning and what the other innovative financial instruments were ; Challenged that the real issue is constrained access to forex and the absence of contract enforcement rather than access to markets and finance, and questioned how much impact the lab can make amid a macroeconomic crisis of balance of payments deficit, external debt burden, inflation and depreciated currency.

a918.speaker: John Heche, Vice Chairman of Chadema
a918.name: John Heche
a918.title: Vice Chairman of Chadema
a918.speech: Said that if the party comes to power it will put in place policies and a better investment environment in the industrial sector, saying this is the right way to end the youth unemployment problem ; addressing a public rally in Singida on 9 June 2025, said that if the party wins the mandate to form a government it will direct major efforts to investment in industries that process and use raw materials from crops, livestock and fisheries.

a918.speaker: John Heche, Vice Chairman of Chadema
a918.name: John Heche
a918.title: Vice Chairman of Chadema
a918.speech: Said that, recognising the importance of industries for employment and national economic development, the First Phase Government under the late Father of the Nation, Mwalimu Julius Nyerere, invested effort and money in building cotton-ginning factories, textile factories and plants for other agricultural and livestock products, industries that he said have died for lack of policy and a good management plan: “In Arusha we had the General Tyres tyre factory, we had a farm-implements factory as well as several cotton-processing factories. These industries did not only provide jobs for Tanzanians, they also stimulated the country’s economy by keeping money in the country.” ; said that many of the industries built during Mwalimu Nyerere’s time have now been privatised and handed into the hands of foreigners who have turned them into warehouses while Tanzanians’ jobs are lost.

a918.speaker: John Heche, Vice Chairman of Chadema
a918.name: John Heche
a918.title: Vice Chairman of Chadema
a918.speech: “Right now there are motorcycles in every street and village in the country, but we import even bicycle tyres from abroad. We must make changes that will enable us to get leaders who are chosen by the people’s vote and who will be accountable to the voters.”

a918.speaker: John Heche, Vice Chairman of Chadema
a918.name: John Heche
a918.title: Vice Chairman of Chadema
a918.speech: Said productive agriculture is another area that should be used to create jobs and improve the economy and people’s lives: “In Tanzania we have been blessed with vast fertile land, rainy seasons, lakes and rivers that flow with water all year round, yet we still spend billions of shillings importing cooking oil and wheat from abroad. If Chadema comes to power we will change this situation by putting in place policies and a better investment environment for industries.” ; claimed that, according to government statistics, the nation spends more than Sh260 billion a year importing cooking oil from abroad, money that would have been used to implement development projects if the nation were self-sufficient in oil: “Despite the good valleys suitable for agriculture, Tanzania still spends more than Sh500 billion importing wheat from abroad.”

a918.speaker: John Heche, Vice Chairman of Chadema
a918.name: John Heche
a918.title: Vice Chairman of Chadema
a918.speech: Urged Tanzanians to support the demands for changes that would restore power and authority to the public to elect and hold leaders accountable, unlike the current situation in which those in power decide who becomes a leader.

a918.speaker: John Mnyika, Acting Secretary General of Chadema
a918.name: John Mnyika
a918.title: Acting Secretary General of Chadema
a918.speech: Thanked the public for responding to the party’s ‘No reforms, no election’ campaign, which aims to demand changes to the law and the electoral system so as to level the political playing field for candidates of all parties.

a1172.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (post on Truth Social)
a1172.name: Donald Trump
a1172.title: US President (post on Truth Social)
a1172.speech: Warned Iran on Sunday that the American army would respond with "all its force" if it attacked the United States: "If we are attacked in any way by Iran, the full strength and might of the US armed forces will come down on you at levels never seen before." He reaffirmed on Truth Social that Washington "had nothing to do" with the ongoing Israeli attacks against Tehran.

a1172.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1172.name: Donald Trump
a1172.title: US President
a1172.speech: "We can easily reach a deal between Iran and Israel and end this bloody conflict" ; he had said he was aware of the Israeli operation before it began early on Friday.

a1172.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1172.name: Donald Trump
a1172.title: US President
a1172.speech: On Friday, the American president had urged Tehran to conclude a deal or face "even more brutal" attacks from Israel.

a1172.speaker: Tehran (Iranian authorities)
a1172.name: Tehran (Iranian authorities)
a1172.speech: According to Tehran, the Israeli operation targeted Iranian nuclear and military sites, killing dozens of people, including senior army commanders and atomic scientists.

a1172.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a1172.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
a1172.title: Israeli Prime Minister
a1172.speech: Promised to strike "all the targets of the ayatollahs' regime".

a1233.speaker: Choguel Maiga, former Prime Minister of Mali
a1233.name: Choguel Maiga
a1233.title: former Prime Minister of Mali
a1233.speech: publicly denounced the military for a lack of clarity over when it would hand over power to a civilian government, before being sacked in November 2024.

a1233.speaker: Cheick Oumar Konare, Choguel Maiga’s lawyer
a1233.name: Cheick Oumar Konare
a1233.title: Choguel Maiga’s lawyer
a1233.speech: told the AFP news agency that no date has yet been set for the former leader’s trial ; “We believe in justice, we are calm while awaiting the trial,” explaining that Maiga would remain in prison for the trial.

a1233.speaker: Public prosecutor of Mali (statement)
a1233.name: Public prosecutor of Mali (statement)
a1233.speech: said the charges against Maiga involve “money laundering equal to many billions of CFA francs”, or several million US dollars.

a1233.speaker: AFP news agency
a1233.name: AFP news agency
a1233.speech: reported that the former prime minister was arrested one week ago, days after Mali’s military leaders carried out dozens of arrests to quash an alleged plot within the army’s ranks to topple the government; reported, citing a judicial source, that nine of Maiga’s colleagues from his time as prime minister also appeared before the court on Tuesday, with two being charged, some acquitted and others still awaiting their hearing.

a1233.speaker: Moussa Mara, former Prime Minister of Mali (social media post)
a1233.name: Moussa Mara
a1233.title: former Prime Minister of Mali (social media post)
a1233.speech: was imprisoned after tweeting his support for jailed critics of the military.

a1233.speaker: Human Rights Watch
a1233.name: Human Rights Watch
a1233.speech: according to it, up to 350,000 people are currently displaced by the fighting in Mali.

a1233.speaker: Choguel Maiga, former Prime Minister of Mali
a1233.name: Choguel Maiga
a1233.title: former Prime Minister of Mali
a1233.speech: previously said he believed the military would safeguard the country’s democracy: “We must refound the Malian state, so that no political power can ever again create the conditions for a return to an unconstitutional order!” he told Al Jazeera in an interview in 2023.

a1233.speaker: Choguel Maiga, former Prime Minister of Mali
a1233.name: Choguel Maiga
a1233.title: former Prime Minister of Mali
a1233.speech: since his dismissal has become one of the military’s fiercest critics, accusing it of weaponising the courts to silence dissent.

a1233.speaker: Alioune Tine, former United Nations rapporteur on Mali to the Security Council
a1233.name: Alioune Tine
a1233.title: former United Nations rapporteur on Mali to the Security Council
a1233.speech: said “If the most prominent opposition leaders are arrested and imprisoned, including Choguel, who once gave the junta credibility, then I believe today the junta credibility is greatly weakened.”

a1264.speaker: USAID (statement on its website)
a1264.name: USAID (statement on its website)
a1264.speech: The agency said in a statement on its website that thousands of employees will be placed on leave from Friday night. In the announcement, USAID said all "direct-hire personnel" will be placed on leave at the end of this week except those on "mission-critical functions, core leadership and specially designated programs". USAID said it would work with the State Department to arrange and pay for return travel for its many personnel posted outside the US within the month. Those employees who are part of the exceptions will be told by 15:00 EDT on Thursday. The statement concludes with the message: "Thank you for your service."

a1264.speaker: USAID (email to staffers, obtained by BBC News)
a1264.name: USAID (email to staffers
a1264.title: obtained by BBC News)
a1264.speech: Many USAID staffers received an email notifying them they had been placed on paid administrative leave. The email told employees they must remain "available" by telephone and email during business hours but are not allowed to enter USAID buildings.

a1264.speaker: Congressional Research Service (report/data)
a1264.name: Congressional Research Service (report/data)
a1264.speech: According to the Congressional Research Service, the agency, which provides humanitarian aid to more than 100 countries, employs 10,000 people worldwide and two-thirds of those people work overseas; USAID managed more than $40b (£32.25b) in fiscal year 2023.

a1264.speaker: Elon Musk, billionaire Tesla CEO appointed to run a new agency to identify US government spending cuts
a1264.name: Elon Musk
a1264.title: billionaire Tesla CEO appointed to run a new agency to identify US government spending cuts
a1264.speech: Has said USAID should be shut down as it is "beyond repair".

a1264.speaker: Andy Kim, New Jersey Senator
a1264.name: Andy Kim
a1264.title: New Jersey Senator
a1264.speech: "[USAID is] a foreign policy tool with bipartisan origins that is critical in this dangerous global environment," Kim wrote on social media. "Gutting it means gutting our ability to compete and keep America safe."

a1358.speaker: Bank of Uganda (data)
a1358.name: Bank of Uganda (data)
a1358.speech: According to data from Bank of Uganda, Uganda's export earnings have dropped from as high as an average of US$15.6 million monthly in January to an average of US$0.68 million as at the end of December last year.

a1358.speaker: National Bank of Rwanda (statement)
a1358.name: National Bank of Rwanda (statement)
a1358.speech: According to the National Bank of Rwanda, in January 2020, the Rwandan urban consumer price index increased by 0.6% month-to-month, higher than a decrease of 0.3% achieved in the previous month; year-on-year inflation stood at 7.3% for January 2020 compared to 6.7% reached in December 2019. ; "On monthly basis, the inflationary pressures were due to food and non-alcoholic beverages whose prices increased by 0.6% in January from a decrease of 0.3% recorded in the previous month." ; "Prices increased particularly for food products including Irish potato, fermented sorghum, sweet potato, sorghum, palm oil, taro, local rice, live chicken among others. Overall, there was an increase in prices of fresh products (0.3% in January compared to a decrease of 2.8% realized in the previous month)." ; The central bank of Rwanda noted that there would be a "continuing rise in prices of alcoholic beverages and tobacco (21.1% against 20.6% in December) and the uptick in prices of housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels (2.4% after 2.2% in December 2019)."

a1358.speaker: A Rwandan citizen who preferred anonymity
a1358.name: A Rwandan citizen who preferred anonymity
a1358.speech: Told The Independent in November 2019, "Price hikes every now and then. You can imagine the price of 1 kilogramme of beans has doubled its period in a price of three months."

a1358.speaker: A site that aggregates exchange rate movements in the world (data)
a1358.name: A site that aggregates exchange rate movements in the world (data)
a1358.speech: Data from the site shows that the Rwanda Franc has weakened against the US Dollar; from July 2019, the Rwanda Franc steadily loses ground against the US Dollar in the period up to January and the trend had not relented till February.

a1623.speaker: Takele Kuruenda, input supply director at the Oromia Bureau of Agriculture (on allocation)
a1623.name: Takele Kuruenda
a1623.title: input supply director at the Oromia Bureau of Agriculture (on allocation)
a1623.speech: According to him, the volume of fertiliser allocated is low compared to the land to be farmed; Oromia Regional State, which requested 19.9 million quintals, has been allocated 10.5 million quintals, meeting 53pc of its demand.

a1623.speaker: Takele Kuruenda, input supply director at the Oromia Bureau of Agriculture (on prices)
a1623.name: Takele Kuruenda
a1623.title: input supply director at the Oromia Bureau of Agriculture (on prices)
a1623.speech: "We're worried about whether farmers will be able to afford increased prices."

a1623.speaker: Assefa Tilahun (PhD), agricultural economist (on demand and supply)
a1623.name: Assefa Tilahun (PhD)
a1623.title: agricultural economist (on demand and supply)
a1623.speech: "The demand from farmers, including commercial growers, is high. But, supply remains low."

a1623.speaker: Assefa Tilahun (PhD), agricultural economist (on compost and organic fertilisers)
a1623.name: Assefa Tilahun (PhD)
a1623.title: agricultural economist (on compost and organic fertilisers)
a1623.speech: Said that while compost is a sustainable alternative, it is not a quick fix, and producing compost at scale requires resources and training: "It requires a major shift in farming practices. Farmers need immediate solutions to meet their current production needs. The government should support these initiatives with training programs and possibly subsidies."

a1623.speaker: Assefa Tilahun (PhD), agricultural economist (on opening the import sector)
a1623.name: Assefa Tilahun (PhD)
a1623.title: agricultural economist (on opening the import sector)
a1623.speech: "Larger companies could help meet the growing demand for fertiliser if they were allowed to enter the import sector."

a1623.speaker: Leta Legesse, agricultural input director for the Sidama Regional Agriculture Bureau
a1623.name: Leta Legesse
a1623.title: agricultural input director for the Sidama Regional Agriculture Bureau
a1623.speech: "We've 92 unions ready to distribute the fertiliser efficiently."

a1623.speaker: Abera Kedenew, deputy head of the Tigray Bureau of Agriculture
a1623.name: Abera Kedenew
a1623.title: deputy head of the Tigray Bureau of Agriculture
a1623.speech: According to him, Tigray's allocation of one million quintals marks an improvement from last year when the regional state requested 900,000 quintals but was provided only 700,000.

a1623.speaker: Abella Obongo (PhD), agricultural input director of the Gambela Agriculture Bureau
a1623.name: Abella Obongo (PhD)
a1623.title: agricultural input director of the Gambela Agriculture Bureau
a1623.speech: "Most farmers could not access fertiliser due to low quotas last year," he told Fortune.

a1623.speaker: Babekir Halifa, head of the Benishangul Gumuz regional agriculture bureau
a1623.name: Babekir Halifa
a1623.title: head of the Benishangul Gumuz regional agriculture bureau
a1623.speech: "It's climate-smart agriculture that can keep farmland productive for up to three years without additional chemical inputs," on the preparation of four million quintals of compost fertiliser.

a1623.speaker: Kifle Woldemariam, CEO of the Ethiopian Agricultural Business Corporation (EABC)
a1623.name: Kifle Woldemariam
a1623.title: CEO of the Ethiopian Agricultural Business Corporation (EABC)
a1623.speech: According to him, the international fertiliser market has been affected by conflicts, including the ongoing war in Ukraine and instability on the Red Sea corridor; the Corporation has used a price-tracking system to time its procurement and reduce costs: "We'll distribute the fertiliser in November. Previously, we used to distribute stocks in January."

a1623.speaker: Ministry of Agriculture officials
a1623.name: Ministry of Agriculture officials
a1623.speech: According to them, this year's subsidy amount will be determined upon the completion of procurement and reviews of farmers' purchasing power.

a1623.speaker: Mijena Regassa, lead of input distribution at the Oromia Cooperative Promotion Agency
a1623.name: Mijena Regassa
a1623.title: lead of input distribution at the Oromia Cooperative Promotion Agency
a1623.speech: Observed uniform transportation schemes have been lacking, though efforts to digitise the supply chain have helped reduce theft and illicit transportation.

a1623.speaker: Studies (cited)
a1623.name: Studies (cited)
a1623.speech: Show that less than 40pc of farmers use fertiliser, and those who do apply it at rates well below recommended levels.

a1623.speaker: Mengistu Tesfa, lead executive of agricultural input supply at the Ministry of Agriculture
a1623.name: Mengistu Tesfa
a1623.title: lead executive of agricultural input supply at the Ministry of Agriculture
a1623.speech: "Last fiscal year's fertiliser distribution was successful due to effective planning, a new organisational structure, and stakeholder participation"; he believes this year's distribution builds on that success.

a1670.speaker: Commandant Passowendé Pélagie Kabré/Kaboré, Minister of Humanitarian Action and National Solidarity (Burkina Faso)
a1670.name: Commandant Passowendé Pélagie Kabré/Kaboré
a1670.title: Minister of Humanitarian Action and National Solidarity (Burkina Faso)
a1670.speech: Specified that these actions were mainly aimed at the empowerment of the ministry's target populations, namely poor and vulnerable people, internally displaced persons (IDPs), women, people with disabilities and the elderly. According to the minister, about 1.9 million people made up of IDPs, vulnerable populations and disaster victims received food assistance; nearly 80,000 women, including IDPs, were supported in income-generating activities; about 9,000 unaccompanied or separated children received psychosocial care; more than 3,000 girls at risk of or victims of child marriage obtained school scholarships; and more than 1,000 people with disabilities received material support and mobility devices.

a1670.speaker: Commandant Passowendé Pélagie Kabré/Kaboré, Minister of Humanitarian Action and National Solidarity (Burkina Faso)
a1670.name: Commandant Passowendé Pélagie Kabré/Kaboré
a1670.title: Minister of Humanitarian Action and National Solidarity (Burkina Faso)
a1670.speech: Asked about the impact of the suspension of USAID funding, the minister sought to reassure partners and beneficiaries: "We have taken all the necessary measures so that everything we do in the field, we will continue to do."

a1671.speaker: Gregory Bledjian, Head of Mission of Germany to South Sudan
a1671.name: Gregory Bledjian
a1671.title: Head of Mission of Germany to South Sudan
a1671.speech: "Enhancing food and nutritional security, improving education, and fostering social cohesion avert long-term dependence on humanitarian aid. South Sudan has enormous potential to be self-reliant." ; "The second phase of the Joint Resilience Project helps to unlock this potential. Germany is proud to support the South Sudanese people on this trajectory for development."

a1671.speaker: Noala Skinner, UNICEF Representative in South Sudan
a1671.name: Noala Skinner
a1671.title: UNICEF Representative in South Sudan
a1671.speech: "This timely and generous contribution from Germany will have a profound impact on some of the most vulnerable children in South Sudan." ; "It will enable UNICEF to scale up critical interventions – from treating severe malnutrition and ensuring access to clean water, to supporting essential health and education services, and protecting children from harm."

a1671.speaker: Adham Effendi, WFP's Acting Representative and Country Director in South Sudan
a1671.name: Adham Effendi
a1671.title: WFP's Acting Representative and Country Director in South Sudan
a1671.speech: "We are deeply grateful for the support from Germany, whose funding strengthens our commitment to empowering communities in South Sudan." ; "This support is not just aid – it is an investment in lasting resilience, food security, and dignity of the people we serve."

a1741.speaker: Godfrey Shamanena, Chief Nkana of the Lamba people in Lufwanyama (defence filed before the Lusaka High Court Commercial Division)
a1741.name: Godfrey Shamanena
a1741.title: Chief Nkana of the Lamba people in Lufwanyama (defence filed before the Lusaka High Court Commercial Division)
a1741.speech: Denied owing Bowman Lusambo US$105,000, arguing that the former lawmaker had no role in the sale or investment process of Bisma Mining Limited and dismissing Lusambo's claims as baseless and gratuitous ; insisted Mr Lusambo had no legal claim to the money, stressing that he neither facilitated the sale nor invested in the process and that he was not a shareholder or director in Bisma Mining Limited, and that the alleged promise to pay him was merely a gesture of financial help: "The plaintiff never invested any resources nor did he facilitate any negotiations relating to Bisma. In fact, he is neither a shareholder nor a director" ; said he only received a portion of the sale proceeds proportional to his shareholding in Bisma and that the US$165,000 was not disbursed at his request, nor was Mr Lusambo a party to the sale agreement ; contended that any promise to pay Mr Lusambo was not legally binding, as it lacked consideration and was based solely on a personal plea for financial assistance ; asserted that he was wrongly sued, arguing that the entire claim arises from a transaction involving Bisma Mining and Pridegems Mines Limited, to which he was merely a shareholder and not a principal.

a1741.speaker: Bowman Lusambo, former lawmaker (plaintiff, court claim)
a1741.name: Bowman Lusambo
a1741.title: former lawmaker (plaintiff, court claim)
a1741.speech: Sued Chief Nkana in the Lusaka High Court seeking payment of US$105,000, claiming it was his agreed share from the sale of Bisma Mining Limited ; asserted that he had played a key role in facilitating negotiations and investing in legal and commercial efforts that led to the eventual sale of the mine to Grizzly Mining Limited ; said that following the transaction Grizzly Mining, through its chairman Ndiaye Abdoulaye (popularly known as Gunnase), agreed at the request of Chief Nkana to release a balance of US$165,000 from the sale proceeds, to be shared as US$105,000 to himself and US$30,000 each to Chief Nkana and Chieftainess Malembeka ; claimed that Chief Nkana authored a letter confirming this arrangement and instructed Grizzly Mining to disburse the money accordingly, but alleged the full amount was instead deposited into Chief Nkana's personal account.

a1862.speaker: Ali Yusuf Ali-Xoosh, Minister of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation of Somalia
a1862.name: Ali Yusuf Ali-Xoosh
a1862.title: Minister of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation of Somalia
a1862.speech: Emphasized the need for coordinated strategies to provide humanitarian assistance, protection, and durable solutions for refugees and IDPs, and highlighted the government's commitment to ensuring the safety and well-being of displaced individuals and communities.

a1862.speaker: Charles Mballa, Special Representative of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
a1862.name: Charles Mballa
a1862.title: Special Representative of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
a1862.speech: Expressed his appreciation for the ongoing partnership with the Somali government; reiterated UNHCR's dedication to supporting Somalia in addressing the complex displacement crisis; and outlined the various initiatives and programs implemented by UNHCR to assist refugees and IDPs, including efforts to improve living conditions, provide access to essential services, and promote self-reliance and integration.

a1862.speaker: Minister Ali-Xoosh and Charles Mballa (jointly)
a1862.name: Minister Ali-Xoosh and Charles Mballa (jointly)
a1862.speech: Agreed on the importance of strengthening the capacity of national institutions to manage displacement issues effectively, and discussed the need for increased funding and resources to support the government's efforts in providing comprehensive assistance to displaced populations; both leaders reaffirmed the commitment to continue working together to address the challenges faced by refugees and IDPs in Somalia and expressed optimism about the potential for positive outcomes through sustained collaboration and mutual support.

a1869.speaker: Action Against Hunger (NGO)
a1869.name: Action Against Hunger (NGO)
a1869.speech: Told AFP on Tuesday that the impact of US aid cuts has already taken a toll in South Sudan and children are dying.

a1869.speaker: The Lancet (British journal)
a1869.name: The Lancet (British journal)
a1869.speech: On Tuesday, the British Lancet journal projected that the cuts to USAID could lead to more than 14 million deaths by 2030, including over 4.5 million children under the age of five.

a1869.speaker: Denish Ogen Rwot, Action Against Hunger's communication and advocacy lead in South Sudan
a1869.name: Denish Ogen Rwot
a1869.title: Action Against Hunger's communication and advocacy lead in South Sudan
a1869.speech: "I think it's not just a fear. It's already a reality. We're already having some mortality rates coming in" ; "Already we are having children die" ; estimated they had lost 30 percent of their funding due to the USAID cuts: "That means now we'll have facilities without food... and how do we work without these supplies?" ; described how the warehouses in northern Warrap state, near the border with Sudan, were "very empty": "They're still registering people, but there is no food for them" ; "We are running on sheer faith."

a1869.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a1869.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a1869.speech: Warned that acute malnutrition rates among refugee children in South Sudan - fleeing the war in Sudan - had "already breached emergency thresholds."

a2056.speaker: Sebastian !Gobs, Constituency Councillor (Khorixas)
a2056.name: Sebastian !Gobs
a2056.title: Constituency Councillor (Khorixas)
a2056.speech: Confirmed in an interview with nbc News that, as drought persists across the Kunene Region, Khorixas' constituency office is challenged by transport to deliver much-needed food aid to rural residents.

a2071.speaker: Egyptian security sources (anonymous)
a2071.name: Egyptian security sources (anonymous)
a2071.speech: According to them, the country's president Abdel Fattah al-Sissi will not travel to the White House for discussions if the agenda involves U.S. president Donald Trump's proposal to move Palestinians out of Gaza.

a2071.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2071.name: Donald Trump
a2071.title: US President
a2071.speech: Suggested that Gaza should be controlled by the U.S. and turned into the "Riviera of the Middle East" ; has urged Egypt and Jordan to take in Gaza's some 2 million residents, and has warned he may halt aid if they refuse to do so.

a2071.speaker: Egypt (government)
a2071.name: Egypt (government)
a2071.speech: Says Trump issued an open invitation to the country's president earlier this month.

a2071.speaker: The U.S. (government)
a2071.name: The U.S. (government)
a2071.speech: Added that no date for such a visit has been pinned down.

a2071.speaker: King Abdullah II bin Al-Hussein of Jordan
a2071.name: King Abdullah II bin Al-Hussein of Jordan
a2071.speech: Rejected Trump's suggestion to displace Gazans from the enclave.

a2071.speaker: Israel
a2071.name: Israel
a2071.speech: Insisted it would resume fighting if hostages held by Hamas were not freed in the coming days.

a2110.speaker: Abdoulkader Kamil Mohamed, Prime Minister of Djibouti
a2110.name: Abdoulkader Kamil Mohamed
a2110.title: Prime Minister of Djibouti
a2110.speech: Gave an account of his participation in the 4th Edition of the World Food Forum and the "Hand in Hand" Investment Forum, organised by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization, held from 10 to 17 October 2025 in Rome; said these meetings constituted a platform for promoting the national vision of the Republic of Djibouti on (i) food security, (ii) rural development and (iii) nutritional sovereignty, in line with Vision Djibouti 2035 and the Sustainable Development Goals, and reported holding several bilateral meetings on the margins with representatives of the World Food Programme (WFP), the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), and with H.E. Mr Muhammad Yunus, President of the Republic of Bangladesh.

a2110.speaker: Minister of Trade and Tourism of Djibouti
a2110.name: Minister of Trade and Tourism of Djibouti
a2110.speech: Gave a mission report on his participation in the National Day and the Pavilion of the Republic of Djibouti at the Osaka 2025 World Expo in Japan, held from 13 April to 13 October 2025 on the theme "Designing Future Society for Our Lives"; reported that the Djiboutian pavilion had been awarded the Bronze Trophy in the category "Development of the theme of the Osaka 2025 World Expo".

a2110.speaker: Minister of Trade and Tourism of Djibouti
a2110.name: Minister of Trade and Tourism of Djibouti
a2110.speech: Also reported on his participation in the 17th Meeting of the Council of Ministers of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), held from 15 to 16 September 2025 in Cairo, which focused on the operationalisation of the single African market, the harmonisation of regulatory frameworks and the promotion of intra-African trade ; presented the conclusions of the 24th COMESA Summit, held from 8 to 9 October 2025 in Nairobi on the theme "Optimising digitalisation to strengthen regional value chains for sustainable and inclusive growth", which underlined the importance of strengthening digital, logistical and commercial cooperation between member States.

a2110.speaker: Minister Delegate in charge of the Digital Economy and Innovation of Djibouti
a2110.name: Minister Delegate in charge of the Digital Economy and Innovation of Djibouti
a2110.speech: Gave an account of her participation in the Global Gateway Forum 2025, held from 8 to 9 October in Brussels on the theme "Partnerships in a Geopolitical Age".

a2110.speaker: Minister of Youth and Culture of Djibouti
a2110.name: Minister of Youth and Culture of Djibouti
a2110.speech: Gave a progress communication on the preparations for the Pan-African Youth Forum 2025, to be held in Djibouti from 4 to 6 November 2025 on the theme "From Aspiration to Action: Youth as Catalysts of Sustainable Development", organised in partnership with the African Union Commission, saying the Forum aims to make Djibouti a pan-African platform for intergenerational dialogue and co-creation.

a2110.speaker: Secretary General of the Government of Djibouti
a2110.name: Secretary General of the Government of Djibouti
a2110.speech: Gave a report on the African Forum of Official Journals (FAJO) and on the National Exhibition "Heritage Djibouti 2025", held from 15 to 16 October 2025 in Djibouti, saying this first edition, bringing together eighteen African nations, marked a historic step in the consolidation of the governance of law in Africa and highlighted Djibouti's advances in digitisation through the Electronic Official Journal (eJO) ; finally informed the Council that the 2nd edition of the African Forum of Official Journals will be held next year in the Republic of Djibouti.

a2150.speaker: Civil society organisations
a2150.name: Civil society organisations
a2150.speech: Following this year's medium term budget policy statement (MTBPS), raised concerns that diminished funding to provinces, both through the equitable share and through conditional grants, may result in crucial HIV/Aids targets being missed.

a2150.speaker: Jose-Antonio Izazola Licea, UNAids special advisor for resources tracking and finances
a2150.name: Jose-Antonio Izazola Licea
a2150.title: UNAids special advisor for resources tracking and finances
a2150.speech: Warned in 2017 that "with donor support plateauing and expected to decline, the success of South Africa's HIV programme will rest on its ability to mobilise and manage a sustainable flow of domestic resources."

a2150.speaker: Thembisa model (mathematical model of South Africa's HIV epidemic)
a2150.name: Thembisa model (mathematical model of South Africa's HIV epidemic)
a2150.speech: According to the latest outputs, this year 92.4% of people living with HIV knew their status; 71.9% of those diagnosed were on HIV treatment, and 91.2% of those on treatment were virally suppressed ; the model shows that the highest incidence rates are among female sex workers and men who have sex with men (MSM), and version 4.3 estimated a Prep coverage rate of only 3% and 1% in female sex workers and MSM, respectively.

a2150.speaker: Health activists
a2150.name: Health activists
a2150.speech: Have called for closer interrogation of the effectiveness of the HIV conditional grant.

a2150.speaker: Yogan Pillay, former deputy director-general in the national department of health
a2150.name: Yogan Pillay
a2150.title: former deputy director-general in the national department of health
a2150.speech: "These groups require special attention with respect to prevention and significantly increased access to treatment."

a2150.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a2150.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a2150.title: President of South Africa
a2150.speech: In 2019 launched an HIV programme for sex workers and declared that "sex work is work".

a2150.speaker: HIV/Aids life skills conditional grant (strategic goals document)
a2150.name: HIV/Aids life skills conditional grant (strategic goals document)
a2150.speech: Some of the strategic goals of the conditional grant include "addressing social and structural drivers of HIV" and to "contribute to preventing new HIV, STIs, and TB infections".

a2150.speaker: Supplementary budget review (June 2020)
a2150.name: Supplementary budget review (June 2020)
a2150.speech: Accounting for the reduction, it explained that "all planned training sessions for over 20 000 educators [were] cancelled" last year.

a2150.speaker: Research from around the world, including South Africa
a2150.name: Research from around the world
a2150.title: including South Africa
a2150.speech: Has found that effective comprehensive sexuality education programmes delivered by well-trained teachers result in improved knowledge about HIV and pregnancy prevention; decreased sexual risk-taking; the prevention of learners having multiple concurrent sexual partners; improved attitudes towards sexual refusal and condom use and delayed sexual debut.

a2150.speaker: Mbali Baduza (Section27) and Julia Chaskalson (Section27), authors
a2150.name: Mbali Baduza (Section27) and Julia Chaskalson (Section27)
a2150.title: authors
a2150.speech: Argued that National Treasury has failed to provide clear information or concrete plans to assist provinces to meet their HIV programme targets amid budget constraints, and that cuts to the grant and a lack of investment in comprehensive sexuality education and in specialised services for key populations undermine the possibility of "an end to Aids" - and to a future where no one is left behind.

a2191.speaker: Hazrat Mirza Masroor Ahmad, His Holiness (Head of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community)
a2191.name: Hazrat Mirza Masroor Ahmad
a2191.title: His Holiness (Head of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community)
a2191.speech: Said that he would continue mentioning expeditions from the life of the Holy Prophet (sa); said that there was the Expedition of Abdullah bin Rawahah (ra) which took place in Shawwal 6 AH, and that when Abu Rafi' was killed, the Jews appointed Usair bin Rizam as their leader, who announced that he would be different from previous Jewish leaders and that the Holy Prophet (sa) would not be victorious over the Jews on his watch, and who started visiting different Jewish tribes to incite them to fight against the Holy Prophet (sa); said that then there was the Expedition of Amr bin Umayyah Damri which was sent towards Abu Sufyan; said that he would continue mentioning these incidents in the future.

a2191.speaker: Hazrat Mirza Bashir Ahmad (quoted from The Life and Character of the Seal of Prophets (sa), Vol. 3)
a2191.name: Hazrat Mirza Bashir Ahmad (quoted from The Life and Character of the Seal of Prophets (sa)
a2191.title: Vol. 3)
a2191.speech: Writes: "When the Holy Prophet (sa) was informed of these circumstances, he immediately sent an Ansari companion named Abdullah bin Rawahah (ra) along with three other companions to Khaibar, and instructed them to travel stealthily, ascertain intelligence as to the state of affairs and return quickly..." — detailing how the party gathered intelligence, the discourse with Usair bin Rizam, the journey towards Madinah, Usair's treachery at Qarqarah and the ensuing fighting in which no Muslim life was lost while every Jew was annihilated.

a2191.speaker: Hazrat Mirza Bashir Ahmad (quoted from The Life and Character of the Seal of Prophets (sa), Vol. 3)
a2191.name: Hazrat Mirza Bashir Ahmad (quoted from The Life and Character of the Seal of Prophets (sa)
a2191.title: Vol. 3)
a2191.speech: Writes on the dating of the Expedition of Amr bin Umayyah Damri: "There is a disagreement amongst historians with regards to the date of this expedition. Ibni Hisham and Tabari have recorded it in 4 A.H., but Ibni Sa'd has written it to be in 6 A.H. Allamah Qustalani and Zurqani have given precedence to the narration of Ibni Sa'd, therefore, I have also mentioned it among the accounts of 6 A.H. Indeed, Allah knows best. Baihaqi has also supported the details of the account mentioned by Ibni Sa'd, but from this account one cannot establish the period in which it took place."

a2191.speaker: Hazrat Mirza Bashir Ahmad (quoted from The Life and Character of the Seal of Prophets (sa), Vol. 3)
a2191.name: Hazrat Mirza Bashir Ahmad (quoted from The Life and Character of the Seal of Prophets (sa)
a2191.title: Vol. 3)
a2191.speech: Writes that the recollection of their disgraceful failure in the Ghazwah of Ahzab inflamed the Quraish of Makkah, that Abu Sufyan secretly consolidated a plan to assassinate the Holy Prophet (sa), that the would-be assassin was subdued in Madinah by Usaid bin Hudair (ra) and later became a Muslim, and that the Holy Prophet (sa) thereafter sent Amr bin Umayyah Damri (ra) and Salmah bin Aslam (ra) to Makkah, on whose return one Quraish spy was killed and the other taken prisoner.

a2191.speaker: Kharijah bin Husail, a non-Muslim who came to Madinah from Khaibar
a2191.name: Kharijah bin Husail
a2191.title: a non-Muslim who came to Madinah from Khaibar
a2191.speech: "I have left Usair in such a state that he is mustering his armies to strike Madinah."

a2191.speaker: The Jewish ministers consulted by Usair bin Rizam
a2191.name: The Jewish ministers consulted by Usair bin Rizam
a2191.speech: "We do not believe that Muhammad (sa) will accept you as the leader of Khaibar."

a2191.speaker: Usair bin Rizam, leader of the Jews of Khaibar
a2191.name: Usair bin Rizam
a2191.title: leader of the Jews of Khaibar
a2191.speech: "You have no idea. Muhammad (sa) is fed up by this war, and in his heart he desires to bring this course of conflict to an end at any expense."

a2191.speaker: Abdullah bin Anis Ansari (ra)
a2191.name: Abdullah bin Anis Ansari (ra)
a2191.speech: "O enemy of God! Do you wish to betray us?"

a2191.speaker: The Holy Prophet (sa)
a2191.name: The Holy Prophet (sa)
a2191.speech: Thanked God for the safe and peaceful return of the Muslims and said: "Thank God for having saved you from this cruel nation."

a2191.speaker: The Holy Prophet (sa)
a2191.name: The Holy Prophet (sa)
a2191.speech: Said of the approaching stranger, "This man has come with an evil intention"; and after the man was subdued inquired of him, "Tell me truthfully, who are you and with which intention have you come?", and on his asking that his life be spared said, "Yes, relate the entire account truthfully and you shall be forgiven."

a2191.speaker: Abu Sufyan, chief of Makkah
a2191.name: Abu Sufyan
a2191.title: chief of Makkah
a2191.speech: Addressed a few young men of the Quraish of similar interests, saying, "Do you know that Muhammad [sa] freely roams the streets and alleys of Madinah?"; and told the young Bedouin who volunteered, "Enough, enough. You are the man we seek", emphatically reminding him not to disclose this secret to anyone.

a2191.speaker: The young Bedouin man who volunteered to assassinate the Holy Prophet (sa)
a2191.name: The young Bedouin man who volunteered to assassinate the Holy Prophet (sa)
a2191.speech: "I have heard your proposition and I am willing to do this. I am a strong hearted and mature individual, whose grip is severe and whose strike is sudden. If you appoint me to this task and assist me, I am ready to set out in order to kill Muhammad (sa). I have a dagger, which shall remain like the hidden wings of a wild vulture. I shall attack Muhammad (sa) and then run to join a caravan and the Muslims shall not be able to catch me. Furthermore, I am also very proficient in the streets of Madinah."

a2191.speaker: Various Christian historians
a2191.name: Various Christian historians
a2191.speech: Have alleged that the party of Abdullah bin Rawahah (ra) brought Usair, etc. out of Khaibar with the intention that whenever they found the opportunity en-route, they would kill them.

a2191.speaker: Hazrat Mirza Masroor Ahmad, His Holiness (Head of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community)
a2191.name: Hazrat Mirza Masroor Ahmad
a2191.title: His Holiness (Head of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community)
a2191.speech: Said that he constantly draws attention towards prayers for Pakistan, where conditions from time to time become very extreme; said it seems that the government is in the hands of the extremists, and that just yesterday, under the guise of wanting to build a road and under the influence of clerics, an entire mosque of the Ahmadiyya Community, built even before the partition of India and Pakistan, was bulldozed and destroyed; said it is only Allah the Almighty who can swiftly take such people to task and turn their actions back onto them, and that Ahmadis must focus a great deal on prayers.

a2191.speaker: Hazrat Mirza Masroor Ahmad, His Holiness (Head of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community)
a2191.name: Hazrat Mirza Masroor Ahmad
a2191.title: His Holiness (Head of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community)
a2191.speech: Said that in relation to Palestine, it is said that an agreement is in place, yet there are still incidents taking place; said that some people are rejoicing over the agreement, however the forces of the antichrist cannot be trusted at all as they say one thing and do another; said there is no need to become so happy, rather the focus should be on increased prayers, and that Muslims should use wisdom in attaining their rights, may Allah the Almighty enable them to do so.

a2191.speaker: Hazrat Mirza Masroor Ahmad, His Holiness (Head of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community)
a2191.name: Hazrat Mirza Masroor Ahmad
a2191.title: His Holiness (Head of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community)
a2191.speech: Said that he would mention a few deceased members of the Community whose funeral prayers he would lead in absentia — Sheikh Mubarak Ahmad, Nazir Diwan in Rabwah, of whose devotion and service he attested, and Muhammad Munir Adelvi of Qatar — and prayed that may Allah grant them forgiveness and mercy, elevate their station and enable their children to carry on the legacy of their virtues.

a2299.speaker: Sudan Ministry of Health (statement)
a2299.name: Sudan Ministry of Health (statement)
a2299.speech: reported on Tuesday 91,034 cholera cases, including 2,302 deaths, across 116 localities in 17 states, since the outbreak of the epidemic last July. Between July 12 and 18, a total of 1,307 cholera cases were recorded, including 18 deaths, across 35 localities in 12 states, the ministry said in a statement. Tawila locality in North Darfur State recorded the highest number of infections with 519 cases during the week, while Bileil locality in South Darfur State reported the highest number of deaths, according to the ministry.

a2299.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a2299.name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a2299.speech: recently warned that the humanitarian crisis in Sudan is worsening amid the deadly cholera outbreak, floods, and mass returns to underserved areas. ; In South Kordofan State, OCHA, citing local sources, reported that clashes erupted on Tuesday in the besieged city of Kadugli, which is the state capital.

a2299.speaker: Stephane Dujarric, spokesman for UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres
a2299.name: Stephane Dujarric
a2299.title: spokesman for UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres
a2299.speech: has said the UN continues to be gravely concerned about the worsening humanitarian catastrophe and tightening access constraints across Sudan, particularly in the Kordofan region, where hostilities continue to escalate. ; "Armed individuals reportedly attempted to seize food from the main market. As Sudan's hunger crisis deepens, the city remains cut off from humanitarian assistance, with the last supply route from neighbouring North Kordofan now blocked."

a2299.speaker: Stephane Dujarric, spokesman for UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres
a2299.name: Stephane Dujarric
a2299.title: spokesman for UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres
a2299.speech: "Roads connecting the state capital Geneina, which is, as you well know, located next to the crucial Adre border crossing with Chad, the road from Geneina to Mornei and Zalingei, in Central Darfur State, are now impassable." ; "Both of these towns are hosting large numbers of displaced people. UN humanitarian partners warn that continued rains may further cut off access into Central and South Darfur states, making it even more difficult to reach people who need help so desperately."

a2299.speaker: Stephane Dujarric, spokesman for UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres
a2299.name: Stephane Dujarric
a2299.title: spokesman for UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres
a2299.speech: said that in North Darfur State, displaced communities and host families in the town of Tawila have come together to establish community kitchens, which are now feeding thousands of people who fled violence in El Fasher. ; "These kitchens have become a vital lifeline for those without any other access to food. However, they face chronic and severe funding shortfalls. Many of these are struggling to stay open, and some risk shutting down altogether due to lack of resources." ; "As the Spokesman for the Secretary-General mentioned yesterday, the UN and its partners are planning a major scale-up of support for people in Tawila, which requires $120 million over the next three months."

a2299.speaker: Stephane Dujarric, spokesman for UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres
a2299.name: Stephane Dujarric
a2299.title: spokesman for UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres
a2299.speech: "Humanitarian access is further complicated by checkpoint taxes, by roadblocks, and bureaucratic hurdles imposed by local authorities, including requirements for multiple levels of approval to establish the most basic services for the population." ; He said that the UN appeals for unimpeded humanitarian access across Sudan, more international funding to scale up the response, the protection of civilians and aid workers, and an immediate cessation of hostilities.

a2305.speaker: LootLove (Luthando Shosha), TV presenter and radio host
a2305.name: LootLove (Luthando Shosha)
a2305.title: TV presenter and radio host
a2305.speech: tells Drum that when she couldn’t handle it anymore, she took a hiatus and urges everyone to take a break from social media when it’s necessary: "A lot of us are afraid to leave social media platforms, but it’s important to step away from things that no longer serve you or take a break. I don’t post as much as I used to, there’s so much pressure to do certain things or be a certain way. We’ve been taught to constantly post but if it’s too much, leave the platform, and you’ll be fine." ; She shares that she lost a job or two but the "next one will always come".

a2305.speaker: LootLove (Luthando Shosha), host of Honey TV’s Battle of The Ankara
a2305.name: LootLove (Luthando Shosha)
a2305.title: host of Honey TV’s Battle of The Ankara
a2305.speech: "It feels really good to be back in this kind of space, it’s exciting, big and I can’t wait for everybody to watch the show and fall in love with the contestants. We are looking for the best designer on the continent. It’s completely different from anything I have hosted before and I think putting together my love for fashion and my love for TV is really fun and exciting," she says ; LootLove says any space where you get to experience a different way of doing your job and exploring your passion is always welcomed.

a2305.speaker: LootLove (Luthando Shosha), face of the Krone Night Nectar campaign
a2305.name: LootLove (Luthando Shosha)
a2305.title: face of the Krone Night Nectar campaign
a2305.speech: "To get to a place where they trust me with their product, trust me to carry it the way they need it to be carried and to put it in the market the way they needed is a beautiful honour.
