Partnering with them was easy and it came at the right time, it’s another opportunity for me to make my kids proud," Luthando says.

a2305.speaker: LootLove (Luthando Shosha), TV presenter and radio host
a2305.name: LootLove (Luthando Shosha)
a2305.title: TV presenter and radio host
a2305.speech: "I am eternally grateful for these opportunities, not everyone has them right now. I am just really grateful for the opportunity to keep my household going, take care of my kids, and continue to take care of myself and make them proud," she says ; "Before the pandemic, we were quite spoilt, but this reset has given us the ability to look deeper into things. It has been tough but also incredibly enlightening and rewarding. Coming out of this very difficult time; so much has changed, our perspective on life has changed. The things that we value are completely different." ; "When things come to you, you have a completely different understanding of what they mean, the weight that they carry, the blessings they bring to your life and you appreciate it that much more," she says.

a2305.speaker: LootLove (Luthando Shosha), mother of twin girls
a2305.name: LootLove (Luthando Shosha)
a2305.title: mother of twin girls
a2305.speech: She shares that she wants to make them proud ; "We are modern moms. We work, we have careers, we do all these things, and it’s not easy. Half the time I don’t know if I’m doing it right but I am thankful for the support. My family, friends, and nanny, who is like the second mom to my children," she says ; On maintaining a balance, she says it’s all in managing her time well: "You have to be intentional with how you manage your schedule. I have been very blessed to be able to spend a lot of time with my kids. Even in the moments where the work has been quiet, it’s given me more time to get to know my little beings of light."

a2305.speaker: LootLove (Luthando Shosha), presenter of Apple Music’s Africa Now Radio
a2305.name: LootLove (Luthando Shosha)
a2305.title: presenter of Apple Music’s Africa Now Radio
a2305.speech: She says this is one of the best jobs she has ever gotten in her life ; "It’s been so beautiful, eye-opening, educational, and excellent." ; "I work with a brilliant team and that forces me to be brilliant. All my radio experience prepared me for this moment. Even working under Covid-19 regulations, it’s been one of the most magical moments I have ever had," Lootlove says ; "Understanding music from a pan African context has been beautiful. I grew up in South Africa, worked in the SA music industry, there’s quite a lot I didn’t know, so opening that up has been excellent and just what I needed at this point in my life," she shares.

a2305.speaker: LootLove (Luthando Shosha), first South African to host Africa Now Radio
a2305.name: LootLove (Luthando Shosha)
a2305.title: first South African to host Africa Now Radio
a2305.speech: On being the first South African to host the show, she says it’s cool but she hopes she’s not the last: "I want so many other SA broadcasters to have the same opportunities because it’s mind-blowing what happens when you are in that space. I can’t wait to see more South Africans on Apple music taking over, doing amazing things, and capturing the world. It’s happening already," Lootlove says.

a2305.speaker: LootLove (Luthando Shosha), TV presenter and radio host
a2305.name: LootLove (Luthando Shosha)
a2305.title: TV presenter and radio host
a2305.speech: And on what her fans can expect from her, she says wait and see: "I know I have been very quiet and I stepped back a bit but everyone must not panic I’m coming out now, I’ll be making lots of noise."

a2418.speaker: Humanitarian workers / aid groups
a2418.name: Humanitarian workers / aid groups
a2418.speech: Warned that the Trump administration's sweeping foreign aid cuts will send tuberculosis cases and deaths soaring around the world; one told AFP that people are already dying from a lack of treatment in the war-torn Democratic Republic of Congo.

a2418.speaker: Elon Musk, billionaire advisor to President Trump
a2418.name: Elon Musk
a2418.title: billionaire advisor to President Trump
a2418.speech: Has boasted of putting the vast US humanitarian agency USAID "through the woodchipper."

a2418.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a2418.name: Marco Rubio
a2418.title: US Secretary of State
a2418.speech: Announced on Monday that 83% of all USAID contracts were officially cancelled.

a2418.speaker: World Health Organisation
a2418.name: World Health Organisation
a2418.speech: Warned last week that the cuts would endanger millions of lives, pointing out that tuberculosis (TB) efforts averted 3.65 million deaths last year alone.

a2418.speaker: Maxime Lunga, head of local group Club des Amis (DRC), TB survivor
a2418.name: Maxime Lunga
a2418.title: head of local group Club des Amis (DRC), TB survivor
a2418.speech: Said that in the Democratic Republic of Congo, many frontline community workers have been forced to stop helping tuberculosis patients ; "The chaotic situation is starting to get scary here." ; "We know that some of the patients on waiting lists are now dying because they are not being treated."

a2418.speaker: Olya Klymenko, TB People Ukraine
a2418.name: Olya Klymenko
a2418.title: TB People Ukraine
a2418.speech: Lamented that the money had been wasted on a programme to teach children about the dangers of tuberculosis in Ukraine that was three days from starting when the US stop-work order came; it was, she said, a "very bad deal"; she feared the US cuts would reverse the gains made since she survived TB a decade ago ; "People will suffer a lot."

a2418.speaker: Lucica Ditiu, Executive Director of the Stop TB Partnership
a2418.name: Lucica Ditiu
a2418.title: Executive Director of the Stop TB Partnership
a2418.speech: Said the Geneva-based NGO received a letter from the US government terminating all funding late last month and had to share the bad news with 150 community organisations, then received a new letter last week rescinding the termination: "The new letter clearly indicates that all work should resume as planned"; added it was still unclear whether the decision was permanent - or when any new US money would actually be released.

a2418.speaker: Lucica Ditiu, Executive Director of the Stop TB Partnership
a2418.name: Lucica Ditiu
a2418.title: Executive Director of the Stop TB Partnership
a2418.speech: Warned that allowing airborne TB to go untested and untreated could have a "snowball effect" across the world and feared the US cuts could result in a bug that no treatment can stop: "Interrupting a treatment for a drug-resistant TB person is horrible, because it will create a bug that will be spread through the air, so me and you and our families or friends can get it"; added the funding cuts were particularly "devastating" because 2024 was the "best year ever" for the fight against TB.

a2418.speaker: Internal USAID memo by a now-dismissed assistant administrator (published in the New York Times)
a2418.name: Internal USAID memo by a now-dismissed assistant administrator (published in the New York Times)
a2418.speech: The aid cuts will cause rates of tuberculosis and drug-resistant TB to both surge by roughly 30%; "The US will see more cases of hard-to-treat TB arriving at its doorstep."

a2418.speaker: Humanitarian source in Geneva (anonymous)
a2418.name: Humanitarian source in Geneva (anonymous)
a2418.speech: Told AFP the situation was "very dangerous, even for the European Union" because of the risk linked to drug-resistant TB in Ukraine and Georgia.

a2470.speaker: Governor of the Central Bank of The Gambia
a2470.name: Governor of the Central Bank of The Gambia
a2470.speech: Has made it evident that the low earnings from exports are being cushioned by the high level of remittances rising up to D45.6 billion dalasi in 2023.

a2640.speaker: Dr. Stefan Buchwald, Germany's Ambassador to Benin
a2640.name: Dr. Stefan Buchwald
a2640.title: Germany's Ambassador to Benin
a2640.speech: Said the mechanism intends to “support the Beninese government in delivering services and ensuring the security of the population in a flexible, adaptive manner... Together, we aim to support the efforts of the Beninese State to consolidate its presence in the country's strategic regions in order to prevent terrorist violence, counter the spread of instability and improve the resilience of local populations in northern Benin,” recalling that the challenges to be overcome in the regions of northern Benin are multidimensional.

a2640.speaker: Dr. Marcel A. Baglo, Director General of ABeGIEF (Beninese Agency for the Integrated Management of Border Areas)
a2640.name: Dr. Marcel A. Baglo
a2640.title: Director General of ABeGIEF (Beninese Agency for the Integrated Management of Border Areas)
a2640.speech: Explains that the aim is to strengthen the presence of the Beninese State in border localities so as to bring the population from a feeling of abandonment to a feeling of belonging: “That is what we call stabilisation…”

a2640.speaker: Brian Shukan, United States Ambassador to Benin
a2640.name: Brian Shukan
a2640.title: United States Ambassador to Benin
a2640.speech: Welcomed that the actions carried out through the programme contribute “to strengthening the presence of the Beninese State and improving community relations…”

a2640.speaker: Frislain Isidor, Manager of the M-SEC programme
a2640.name: Frislain Isidor
a2640.title: Manager of the M-SEC programme
a2640.speech: “The handover of the desk-benches to various schools in the commune of Materi marks the strengthening of the collaboration between ABeGIEF and M-SEC and the commitment to the stability of our communities in northern Benin.”

a2640.speaker: Alassane Seidou, Minister of the Interior and Public Security of Benin
a2640.name: Alassane Seidou
a2640.title: Minister of the Interior and Public Security of Benin
a2640.speech: Expressed the gratitude of the Executive and of the Beninese people to the initiators of the programme and their partners: “Today's handover of equipment comes in support of national initiatives already under way, and aims to help overcome the material and technical obstacles faced by learners in our border localities with a view to better performance of the Beninese education system,” he added, urging the beneficiaries to make good use of the donation. He also reaffirmed the readiness of his ministerial department to support the implementation of M-SEC.

a2645.speaker: Yoko Kamikawa (Japanese Foreign Minister), Penny Wong (Australia), Subrahmanyam Jaishankar (India) and Antony Blinken (US Secretary of State) – joint declaration
a2645.name: Yoko Kamikawa (Japanese Foreign Minister)
a2645.title: Penny Wong (Australia), Subrahmanyam Jaishankar (India) and Antony Blinken (US Secretary of State) – joint declaration
a2645.speech: “Underlined the importance of a maritime order based on international law, including in the East and South China Seas, and reaffirmed their strong opposition to any unilateral attempt to change the ‘status quo’ by force or coercion.”

a2645.speaker: Quad countries (joint declaration)
a2645.name: Quad countries (joint declaration)
a2645.speech: Also underlined their “firm commitment to creating a free and open Indo-Pacific” ; The Quad countries “showed their commitment to promoting greater concrete efforts in the area of maritime security”, as well as in cybersecurity, the fight against terrorism, emerging technologies and humanitarian and disaster relief assistance, the joint declaration stated ; The four countries also condemned North Korea’s ballistic missile launches, which “destabilise and violate UN Security Council resolutions”, and underlined their commitment to the “complete denuclearisation” of the Korean peninsula.

a2645.speaker: Antony Blinken, US Secretary of State
a2645.name: Antony Blinken
a2645.title: US Secretary of State
a2645.speech: “We are setting the path towards a safer, more secure and more open Indo-Pacific through the strengthening of maritime security and surveillance,” he said during a joint press conference after the meeting. This means “strengthening the capabilities of partners in the region so they know what is happening in each other’s waters,” said Blinken, who pointed, for example, to satellite technology and data-sharing systems that make it possible to interdict illegal fishing operations.

a2645.speaker: Beijing / China
a2645.name: Beijing / China
a2645.speech: Has described the quadrilateral partnership as an “Asian NATO”; Beijing also claims the island of Taiwan as one of its provinces, to be annexed by force if necessary.

a2661.speaker: Press dossier sent to newsrooms (Malian authorities' press kit)
a2661.name: Press dossier sent to newsrooms (Malian authorities' press kit)
a2661.speech: According to the press dossier addressed to the newsrooms, the visit of the President of the Transition to Russia promises to be a key moment for the consolidation of a partnership based on mutual respect, sovereignty and the promotion of shared interests, opening new prospects for the development and stability of Mali and of the AES Confederation.

a2705.speaker: Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research (NMIMR)
a2705.name: Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research (NMIMR)
a2705.speech: The cases of Dengue Fever were conclusively identified at the institute, following the analysis of samples from patients exhibiting acute febrile illnesses.

a2705.speaker: Ghana Health Service, in collaboration with partners including USAID, the World Health Organization (WHO) and UNICEF
a2705.name: Ghana Health Service
a2705.title: in collaboration with partners including USAID, the World Health Organization (WHO) and UNICEF
a2705.speech: Has issued a health alert and is calling for intensified efforts in social and behavioral change initiatives.

a2705.speaker: Ghana Health Service (GHS)
a2705.name: Ghana Health Service (GHS)
a2705.speech: Has emphasized the need for heightened public awareness campaigns on Dengue Fever, focusing on key preventive measures: avoiding mosquito bites by using mosquito nets and wearing protective clothing; eliminating mosquito breeding sites by eliminating standing water and using mosquito repellent; and implementing proper waste management practices around homes and schools ; Urges the public to maintain vigilance and strictly adhere to these preventive measures, and encourages early reporting of symptoms to effectively control the spread of Dengue Fever and safeguard lives.

a2734.speaker: Paul Kagame, President of Rwanda
a2734.name: Paul Kagame
a2734.title: President of Rwanda
a2734.speech: Has expressed support for President Donald Trump’s push to shut down the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID), despite Rwanda being a significant beneficiary of its aid programs: “President Trump has an unconventional way of doing things,” Kagame said in an interview with CNN. “I completely agree with him on many things.” ; when asked about the potential negative impact on Rwanda, which relies on USAID funding for healthcare and development initiatives, Kagame noted, “I think from being hurt, we might learn some lessons.”

a2734.speaker: Paul Kagame, President of Rwanda
a2734.name: Paul Kagame
a2734.title: President of Rwanda
a2734.speech: Emphasized his skepticism towards foreign aid: “It’s an aid thing which I’ve never been a friend of it, much as I’ve been a beneficiary of it” ; echoed sentiments shared by many across Africa that much foreign assistance is lost to corruption or administrative costs rather than reaching those in need ; “African countries need to learn to be self-sufficient. They can’t rely on the generosity of others forever.”

a2734.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2734.name: Donald Trump
a2734.title: US President
a2734.speech: Has consistently criticized USAID as wasteful and inefficient, labeling it as managed by “radical lunatics” during recent media appearances.

a2734.speaker: Global health experts
a2734.name: Global health experts
a2734.speech: Warn about potential disease outbreaks due to reduced funding.

a2823.speaker: Umaro Sissoco Embaló, President of Guinea-Bissau
a2823.name: Umaro Sissoco Embaló
a2823.title: President of Guinea-Bissau
a2823.speech: Outlined his vision for a “stable, secure, and investment-ready” Guinea-Bissau, highlighting priority sectors including energy, agriculture, tourism, technology, and infrastructure; the country's new investment code was presented as a key instrument to attract strong partnerships.

a2823.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, President of Senegal
a2823.name: Bassirou Diomaye Faye
a2823.title: President of Senegal
a2823.speech: Presented his “new vision of cooperation based on trade, mutually beneficial investments, and respect for shared interests” ; underscored Senegal's strengths, including political stability, a favourable business climate, and strategic geographic positioning.

a2823.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, President of Senegal
a2823.name: Bassirou Diomaye Faye
a2823.title: President of Senegal
a2823.speech: At an executive roundtable at the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, in front of about thirty senior executives from major U.S. companies, laid out his “clear, bold, and attractive” economic vision for Senegal ; highlighted recent reforms to improve the business climate and outlined investment opportunities in key sectors such as energy, agribusiness, infrastructure, digital economy, and natural resources (oil and gas).

a2823.speaker: U.S. Chamber of Commerce
a2823.name: U.S. Chamber of Commerce
a2823.speech: Announced the upcoming release of a dedicated Senegal Investment Guide.

a2823.speaker: U.S. investors
a2823.name: U.S. investors
a2823.speech: Expressed strong interest in expanding their presence in Senegal ; praised Gabon's reform agenda and expressed interest in supporting its ambitious initiatives.

a2823.speaker: Christopher Landau, U.S. Deputy Secretary of State and Chairman of the Development Finance Corporation (DFC) Board
a2823.name: Christopher Landau
a2823.title: U.S. Deputy Secretary of State and Chairman of the Development Finance Corporation (DFC) Board
a2823.speech: Conveyed the United States' commitment to boosting economic cooperation with Senegal through increased investment and stronger collaboration between the two countries' private sectors.

a2823.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, President of Liberia
a2823.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a2823.title: President of Liberia
a2823.speech: Focused his remarks on Liberia's rich natural resources, calling for deeper cooperation in the mining sector; expressed Liberia's appreciation for its historic partnership with the U.S., stating: “Liberia has long been a friend of the United States, and we believe in your vision to make America great again.” ; requested support for comprehensive mineral surveys, saying, “Liberia has immense mineral potential, and as a trusted friend, we seek your support to conduct thorough geological assessments. This is essential for unlocking sustainable growth and mutual economic benefit.” ; invited the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) to collaborate on mapping critical minerals nationwide, with a focus on strategic investment opportunities in rare earth elements, lithium, and other essential resources.

a2823.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, President of Liberia
a2823.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a2823.title: President of Liberia
a2823.speech: Reaffirmed Liberia's commitment to transparency, good governance, and the rule of law; presented the ARREST agenda (Agriculture, Roads, Rule of law, Education, Sanitation, and Tourism) as the foundation for economic partnership and national growth.

a2823.speaker: Christopher Landau, U.S. Deputy Secretary of State
a2823.name: Christopher Landau
a2823.title: U.S. Deputy Secretary of State
a2823.speech: Welcomed the recent signing of a Concession and Access Agreement (CAA) with Ivanhoe Liberia Ltd., which secures multi-user access to Liberia's key railway corridor.

a2823.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, President of Liberia (speaking through Ambassador Charles A. Snetter Jr.)
a2823.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a2823.title: President of Liberia (speaking through Ambassador Charles A. Snetter Jr.)
a2823.speech: At a trade conference in Philadelphia, declared: “The era of PowerPoint presentations is over—we're now taking concrete action on the ground. We invite you to join this transformation.” ; also highlighted his country's unanimous election to a non-permanent seat on the UN Security Council, calling it “a powerful signal of Liberia's growing international credibility—and a message to global investors that Liberia is back and open for business.”

a2823.speaker: Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema, President of Gabon
a2823.name: Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema
a2823.title: President of Gabon
a2823.speech: Presented his vision for “building a strong, sovereign, and forward-looking economy,” with a focus on the flagship 901-km Belinga-Boué-Mayumba railway line, designed to transport iron ore and integrate national infrastructure ; announced during his New Year's address on 31 December 2024 that the railway is a cornerstone of Gabon's industrialisation strategy and effort to connect its resources to global value chains.

a2823.speaker: Mohamed Ould Cheikh El-Ghazouani, President of Mauritania
a2823.name: Mohamed Ould Cheikh El-Ghazouani
a2823.title: President of Mauritania
a2823.speech: Emphasised Mauritania's strategic advantages in his meeting with President Trump, expressing his “deep appreciation for the invitation” and applauding “the American president's efforts to promote peace in several regions” ; pointed to Mauritania's strategic location on the Atlantic coast, directly across from the U.S. and linking North and Sub-Saharan Africa; recalled that “for sixty years, Mauritania has been Africa's second-largest iron ore producer,” and stressed the richness of the country's marine resources, especially fish.

a2823.speaker: Mohamed Ould Cheikh El-Ghazouani, President of Mauritania
a2823.name: Mohamed Ould Cheikh El-Ghazouani
a2823.title: President of Mauritania
a2823.speech: Commended President Trump's peace initiatives and called for efforts to end the war in Gaza, noting that the U.S. administration “has played a significant role in fostering peace” in various regions.

a3003.speaker: Lorde (Ella Yelich-O'Connor), New Zealand singer
a3003.name: Lorde (Ella Yelich-O'Connor)
a3003.title: New Zealand singer
a3003.speech: On the song's release she told fans in an email, "Her feet are bare at all times. She's sexy, playful, feral and free. She's a modern girl in a deadstock bikini, in touch with her past and her future, vibrating at the highest level when summer comes around. Her skin is glowing, her lovers are many. I'm completely obsessed with her, and soon you will be too."

a3003.speaker: Lorde (Ella Yelich-O'Connor), New Zealand singer
a3003.name: Lorde (Ella Yelich-O'Connor)
a3003.title: New Zealand singer
a3003.speech: Described her third album as a "celebration of the natural world and an attempt at immortalising the deep, transcendent feelings I have when I'm outdoors" and as "happy, playful music"; revealed that her best friend, Ophelia Mikkelson Jones, took the cover photo of her running in a bikini in a spontaneous moment of joy on the beach.

a3003.speaker: Lorde (Ella Yelich-O'Connor), New Zealand singer
a3003.name: Lorde (Ella Yelich-O'Connor)
a3003.title: New Zealand singer
a3003.speech: "He came over to work in the studio in Auckland and I went to Los Angeles," she told fans last year. "It flowed and a thing started to take shape. Then the world shut down and we FaceTimed."

a3003.speaker: COSMOPOLITAN.COM and INSIDER.COM (cited sources)
a3003.name: COSMOPOLITAN.COM and INSIDER.COM (cited sources)
a3003.speech: Listed as the sources for the article's account of Lorde's new album.

a3063.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) (statement)
a3063.name: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) (statement)
a3063.speech: Acknowledged the recent donation of $32.5 million from the United States government, designated for providing food assistance and nutritional support to internally displaced persons in conflict-affected areas of Nigeria, and recognised contributions from the United Kingdom, the African Development Bank, ECHO, France, Saudi Arabia and the UN Central Emergency Response Fund ; emphasised that the financial support received from the United States government will facilitate emergency food and nutrition assistance for communities adversely affected by conflict in Northeast Nigeria ; "The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) welcomes recent contributions from donors since warning that operations would be forced to shut down in July. This includes new funding from the United States of America to support emergency food and nutrition assistance for communities affected by conflict in Northeast Nigeria."

a3063.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a3063.name: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a3063.speech: Had issued warnings regarding the potential cessation of its operations in Nigeria by the end of July due to funding shortages ; announced in July that it would be forced to suspend all emergency food and nutrition aid for 1.3 million people in North-east Nigeria by the end of July due to "critical funding shortfalls" ; said it urgently requires $130 million to prevent an imminent pipeline break and sustain food and nutrition operations through the end of 2025.

a3063.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a3063.name: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a3063.speech: Indicated that the conflict across Nigeria's northeast and northwest regions has pushed more than 5 million people into acute hunger, and that more than 2.5 million children are "malnourished" ; said the US funding, as well as that of other donors received so far, will keep 187 nutrition clinics open across Borno, Adamawa, and Yobe states, ensuring continued treatment for more than 300,000 malnourished children and mothers ; said support from the United States and other donors will enable WFP to sustain operations over the next three months, reaching 850,000 people in camps and host communities, a significant reduction from the 1.5 million people it assisted in July.

a3063.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) (statement)
a3063.name: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) (statement)
a3063.speech: Said Nigeria, as Africa's largest democracy, plays a critical role in safeguarding regional stability and preventing the spread of insecurity across the Sahel ; "With this funding, WFP will continue to advance humanitarian solutions that drive peace and production, helping to restore Northern Nigeria's potential as the nation's breadbasket."

a3063.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a3063.name: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a3063.speech: "WFP urgently calls on other donors, including the Nigerian Government and private sector, to help close the funding gap and co-invest in the region" ; stated that without additional contributions, their operations will face further cuts, putting millions of people at risk of deepening hunger.

a3063.speaker: David Stevenson, WFP Country Director in Nigeria
a3063.name: David Stevenson
a3063.title: WFP Country Director in Nigeria
a3063.speech: Explained that the contributions came at a pivotal moment for Nigeria and the wider region: "Escalating conflict is driving farmers from their fields. Over the past nine months, WFP and partners have recorded more than three attacks each day on communities across the northeast, with farmers among the hardest hit" ; said the disruption to food production has left families with no means to feed themselves, while those left behind face hunger, displacement, and the risk of recruitment by armed groups.

a3063.speaker: US government
a3063.name: US government
a3063.speech: According to the US government, the assistance includes complementary nutritional support for 41,569 pregnant and breastfeeding women and girls, as well as 43,235 children.

a3063.speaker: PREMIUM TIMES (report)
a3063.name: PREMIUM TIMES (report)
a3063.speech: Reported on Wednesday that the US government donated $32.5 million to WFP to facilitate food assistance and nutritional support to internally displaced individuals in conflict-torn regions of Nigeria.

a3197.speaker: Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET) (report)
a3197.name: Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET) (report)
a3197.speech: Acute food insecurity “crisis (IPC Phase 3) outcomes are expected to persist from October 2024 to January 2025 in areas affected by El Niño-induced drought during the 2023/2024 agricultural season and areas impacted by conflict in the north” ; Places the central and southern regions and the province of Cabo Delgado in the “crisis phase, level three” of food risk ; “This is due to a combination of factors, including the onset of the lean season in October, below-average harvests in 2024, limited income-earning opportunities due to increased competition, and above-average staple food prices” ; These conditions will make it difficult for poor and very poor households with below-average purchasing power to access food ; “In Cabo Delgado, certain areas that receive regular humanitarian food assistance are likely to experience Stressed! (IPC Phase 2!).”

a3197.speaker: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) (statement)
a3197.name: United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) (statement)
a3197.speech: Recently estimated that around 4.8 million people need humanitarian assistance in Mozambique, with US$64 million (€60.6 million) needed to meet the needs: “The multiple crises currently affecting Mozambique – conflict, drought and public health emergencies – are straining humanitarian resources. Some 4.8 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance (10% of people with disabilities), including 3.4 million children.”

a3197.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a3197.name: United Nations (UN)
a3197.speech: Said in September that nearly two million people were in need of humanitarian assistance in the country ; “This year, Mozambique was affected by drought induced by the El Niño phenomenon during the 2023-2024 season. It is estimated that around 1.8 million people could face food insecurity between next October and March 2025. Faced with this situation, the need for humanitarian assistance for the affected communities has been increasing, especially in the central and southern regions of Mozambique.”

a3213.speaker: Julius Malema, leader of a radical left-wing opposition party in South Africa (in video shown)
a3213.name: Julius Malema
a3213.title: leader of a radical left-wing opposition party in South Africa (in video shown)
a3213.speech: Sings “Kill the Boer”, a chant inherited from the struggle against apartheid, the former white-minority regime.

a3213.speaker: Democratic Alliance (centre-right South African party, member of the governing coalition)
a3213.name: Democratic Alliance (centre-right South African party
a3213.title: member of the governing coalition)
a3213.speech: Condemns the chant and is calling for it to be banned.

a3213.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3213.name: Donald Trump
a3213.title: US President
a3213.speech: Said that the dozens of cars in the video carried “entire families” of white farmers fleeing their lands ; “They are being killed,” the American president said ; “Generally, these are white farmers fleeing South Africa, and it is a very sad thing to see. I hope we can have an explanation for this, because I know you do not want it.”

a3213.speaker: Washington (US government)
a3213.name: Washington (US government)
a3213.speech: Reiterated its accusations of “genocide” against white South African farmers, after having welcomed onto its territory Afrikaners designated as “refugees”.

a3213.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a3213.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a3213.title: President of South Africa
a3213.speech: Pretoria firmly rejects these accusations, with Cyril Ramaphosa retorting that “no, nobody can take land”.

a3332.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
a3332.name: Daniel Chapo
a3332.title: President of Mozambique
a3332.speech: Announced that construction of a bridge and ring road in central Mozambique, two of the main projects in a project funded with $500 million from the United States government, will begin in 2026: "We also came here to Mocuba to discuss what we are going to do. We haven't forgotten what we promised here in Mocuba during the election campaign. That's why we came here to say: The bridge over the Licungo River and the Mocuba ring road will begin next year."

a3332.speaker: Millennium Challenge Account (MCA) announcement of December, reported by Lusa
a3332.name: Millennium Challenge Account (MCA) announcement of December
a3332.title: reported by Lusa
a3332.speech: Stated that the MCA planned to launch a tender for the construction of the new bridge over the Licungo River and a ring road early this year, planning to publish a "Specific Tender Announcement" for the project and release the corresponding document "by the end of January 2025" ; "the existing bridge over the Licungo River is congested, has exceeded its useful life, and is no longer fit for purpose. It has been damaged by floods twice since its construction in the 1940s, and there are no practical alternatives for crossing the Licungo River for heavy trucks when it is damaged by floods."

a3332.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) board of directors
a3332.name: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) board of directors
a3332.speech: Announced this financing compact, called the Mozambique Coastal Connectivity and Resilience Compact, the second since 2007.

a3719.speaker: Thiik Thiik Mayardit, Deputy Mayor of Juba City
a3719.name: Thiik Thiik Mayardit
a3719.title: Deputy Mayor of Juba City
a3719.speech: Said in an interview with Eye Radio that the Eritrean ambassador to South Sudan has promised to help in resolving the ongoing strike by water tankers; acknowledged the difficulties faced by Juba residents in obtaining drinking water and admitted that the water crisis has worsened because the price reduction was issued without listening to concerns of water sellers; said efforts are underway to hold consultations with the drivers ; “I talked to the ambassador of Eritrea as most of the drivers are from and I told him that water tankers are not operating. Some citizens had four days and others five days without water.” ; “You don’t do something without having an alternative to the problem. When they summoned him, the mayor told the parliament, are you going to help me in what I’m going to do? However I talked to the ambassador and he confirmed to me that the water tankers would resume work.” ; said the Council is currently negotiating with the water sellers, and they will resume work on Monday after a mutual agreement on the tariff.

a3719.speaker: Eritrean ambassador to South Sudan
a3719.name: Eritrean ambassador to South Sudan
a3719.speech: Promised that the water tankers will soon resume work.

a3719.speaker: Some Juba residents
a3719.name: Some Juba residents
a3719.speech: Said on Sunday they have gone for four days without access to water for domestic use.

a3719.speaker: Water tanker drivers
a3719.name: Water tanker drivers
a3719.speech: Reject the new tariffs, arguing that they are insufficient to cover the rising costs of operating their tankers, including maintenance, fuel, and traffic fees.

a3719.speaker: Augustino Jadalla, Central Equatoria Governor
a3719.name: Augustino Jadalla
a3719.title: Central Equatoria Governor
a3719.speech: On October 5 directed Juba City Council leadership to withdraw the license of water tankers who continue to stay off work amid the ongoing strike ; told the City Council leadership to address pressing issues facing the city, including the resistance of water tankers against its fixed prices as well as waste management and improved service delivery.

a3719.speaker: National parliament of South Sudan
a3719.name: National parliament of South Sudan
a3719.speech: Following deliberations, recommended that the water stakeholders hold a meeting to address the concern and directed relevant parliamentary committees to oversee the implementation of a solution to the rising water cost.

a3848.speaker: Dr. Michael Usi, Vice President of the Republic of Malawi
a3848.name: Dr. Michael Usi
a3848.title: Vice President of the Republic of Malawi
a3848.speech: Commended USAID and its partners for their role in transforming Malawian communities through the Titukulane Project ; Speaking during the close-out ceremony, emphasized the importance of collaborative efforts in addressing national challenges and noted that the project has demonstrated the effectiveness of a proactive approach to tackling environmental and social challenges ; "Since its launch in 2019, the project has shown that unity and commitment can turn challenges into opportunities. By supporting proactive strategies aligned with the National Resilience Strategy (2018-2030), the project has empowered communities to embrace climate-smart agriculture, inclusive governance, and sustainable practices." ; Highlighted the generational impact of the initiative, noting its emphasis on sustainability and its use of research and data to capture the voices of the people.

a3848.speaker: Dr. Michael Usi, Vice President of the Republic of Malawi
a3848.name: Dr. Michael Usi
a3848.title: Vice President of the Republic of Malawi
a3848.speech: Shared observations from the project, highlighting its success in addressing stigma and gender inequality, and praised men from Bimbi and Traditional Authority Kuntumanji in Zomba for their willingness to embrace roles traditionally seen as female.

a3848.speaker: Pamella Kuwali, Director of CARE Malawi
a3848.name: Pamella Kuwali
a3848.title: Director of CARE Malawi
a3848.speech: Reinforced the Vice President's sentiments, describing the Titukulane Project as pivotal in addressing challenges such as climate change and resilience-building.

a4025.speaker: USAID project worker (anonymous, asked not to be named; health worker with wife and three children, Makongo Juu, Dar es Salaam)
a4025.name: USAID project worker (anonymous
a4025.title: asked not to be named; health worker with wife and three children, Makongo Juu, Dar es Salaam)
a4025.speech: Told Mwananchi that he never thought he would fall into the disaster of losing his job, since he had a long-term contract, and that he is going through hardship after missing his January salary because of President Trump’s order: “In January we did not get a salary, so we had to keep going to work as usual. But later we were told to stand down to allow for the 90 days.” ; “I paid the house rent at the beginning of January for the whole year, school fees for the children and other important things, and I was left with no money. My expectation was that the January salary would help me run the family.” ; “For now I have asked the landlord for help to find another tenant so that he can return that rent to me, so I can look for a cheaper house and get some capital for whatever business I can do. I have no certainty of returning to employment, so I am looking for an alternative early.”

a4025.speaker: Another worker at another organisation (anonymous)
a4025.name: Another worker at another organisation (anonymous)
a4025.speech: “We started working from home, and when the end of the month came we were not paid the January salary. We have already begun to taste the hardship because, as you know, January has many demands, and to also miss a salary — we are going through a very hard time.”

a4025.speaker: John Ambrose, psychology expert
a4025.name: John Ambrose
a4025.title: psychology expert
a4025.speech: Said these workers will be affected psychologically because they do not accept what has happened, explaining that the person concerned may experience anger, blame and recrimination and so may do things that are not right; advised them to come to terms with the situation and let life go on.

a4025.speaker: Dr Mugisha Nkoronko, President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
a4025.name: Dr Mugisha Nkoronko
a4025.title: President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
a4025.speech: Called on the Government to make sure it finds a quick solution in order to protect the skills and remove the disruption to citizens: “We recommend urgent steps to rescue this situation; we cannot dodge that responsibility. The Government should go on carrying out an assessment of the impacts and confront them scientifically.”

a4025.speaker: Alexander Baluhya, President of the Tanzania National Nurses Association (TANNA)
a4025.name: Alexander Baluhya
a4025.title: President of the Tanzania National Nurses Association (TANNA)
a4025.speech: Said the departure of many workers at the same time from health facilities is a major challenge that has come at a time when the Nation was not prepared and the workers were not prepared, and that the Government may come up with a plan to rescue the shortfall: “The Government must take responsibility; there was already a shortage, so it will increase. Those affected are not the nurses left with a heavy workload, but the citizens who will not get their services on time. I believe the Government must have an alternative way to see how to reduce this challenge.” ; said the workers are not at fault in any way, so their entitlements must be looked at carefully and administered in line with their contracts.

a4025.speaker: Fadhili Hezekiah, President of the Pharmaceutical Society of Tanzania (PST)
a4025.name: Fadhili Hezekiah
a4025.title: President of the Pharmaceutical Society of Tanzania (PST)
a4025.speech: Said statistics are important for the country to know how many have been affected, and that many pharmacists were in HIV/AIDS projects: “The Government should know how big the shortage is. A thorough assessment of what should be done at this time. Perhaps there are those who were paid 50 per cent by the Government and 50 per cent by the organisations — we should also know this. Perhaps the impact may not be seen directly in research and empowerment, but I believe it will be seen in services.”

a4025.speaker: Regnant Kivinge, chairman of Mafinga Town Council
a4025.name: Regnant Kivinge
a4025.title: chairman of Mafinga Town Council
a4025.speech: Said the Councillors’ Council has set aside 15.6 million shillings for the payment of workers who were being paid by the Benjamin William Mkapa Foundation and the USAID Afya Yangu Programme: “We have made monthly arrangements; after seeing that these organisations had issued a letter of suspension, so that our citizens would not be affected, we had to make the decision to pay from our own internal funds — out of 73 workers we have retained 26 who were working in essential areas.” ; said they chose eight essential areas, especially HIV/AIDS, cervical cancer, family planning and other important ones.

a4025.speaker: Dr Hamad Nyembea, Director of the Curative Services Department, Ministry of Health
a4025.name: Dr Hamad Nyembea
a4025.title: Director of the Curative Services Department, Ministry of Health
a4025.speech: Told Mwananchi on February 12 that an analysis had already been done regarding the shortage that will arise and that facilities had already made adjustments by looking at alternatives: “Whether it is a hospital or a health centre, they have already looked at the areas that will have a shortage and been able to redistribute those workers who are employed by the Government so that they can fill those positions and services are not shaken.”

a4025.speaker: Paschal Mbotta, Siha District Medical Officer
a4025.name: Paschal Mbotta
a4025.title: Siha District Medical Officer
a4025.speech: Answering a question from the council chairman Dancan Urasa, said six workers were the ones affected by that decision and that their jobs have been stalled: “The impact that exists is that six workers at Siha District Hospital have had their contracts terminated after that announcement, but there are others whose number I have not yet obtained; we will follow up in various places including Ashengai and Ngarenairobi in order to get the exact number of workers who will be affected.” ; said those workers have been retained so that they can continue to help patients living with HIV whom they have been following up at their homes and treating.

a4025.speaker: Mark Masue, Acting Executive Director of Siha District Council
a4025.name: Mark Masue
a4025.title: Acting Executive Director of Siha District Council
a4025.speech: Said the director’s office has not received any instructions from the Government: “We are continuing with this arrangement while we await the Government’s instructions on their matter.”

a4112.speaker: Kimberly Rosen, USAID/Ghana Mission Director
a4112.name: Kimberly Rosen
a4112.title: USAID/Ghana Mission Director
a4112.speech: “The United States is proud to partner with the Ghana Health Service to bring health services to remote communities,” said at the handover ceremony. “The boats will improve medical outreach, providing immunizations, maternal and childcare, malaria, nutrition, and other health services to you—the people of Jomoro.”

a4112.speaker: Gabriel Yengliereh, Jomoro District Director of Health Services
a4112.name: Gabriel Yengliereh
a4112.title: Jomoro District Director of Health Services
a4112.speech: emphasized the importance of the boats, noting, “None of the communities along the lagoon have a health facility, and reaching them by road is nearly impossible. With these new boats, we can now bring critical health services directly to these remote communities.”

a4173.speaker: Khanyisa Jaceni, South African musician and content creator
a4173.name: Khanyisa Jaceni
a4173.title: South African musician and content creator
a4173.speech: Shares that Softer is a continuation of her first EP Soft, explaining that, “I feel like I am in another phase of my life where I just want to dive deeper into the softer element of who I am. I just feel grown yabona in that sense but ja, just toning it down a bit. You know how loud amapiano is, so it's just more emphasis of the softer side.”

a4173.speaker: Khanyisa Jaceni, South African musician and content creator
a4173.name: Khanyisa Jaceni
a4173.title: South African musician and content creator
a4173.speech: Reveals that her talent is more of a gift than a skill she's had to hone: “I think it's a gift from God, honestly” ; “I sometimes take moments and just have those lessons impromptu. Also, there's some tricks I learnt from vocal coaches while I was working on Clash of the Choirs, so some techniques here and there. But more than anything, it's not a skill. It's a talent, it's from God, it's all him and I'm so grateful.”

a4173.speaker: Khanyisa Jaceni, South African musician and content creator
a4173.name: Khanyisa Jaceni
a4173.title: South African musician and content creator
a4173.speech: “Come Duze, I'm thinking of shooting it with my man, like a soft launch nyana” ; “I mean, he's been such a big part of my growth. We were with each other before the fame … Even my songs, I would bounce some off of him and he's just like, ‘Oh I like this one. Change this, do this’. So, he's been such a supportive part of my journey and I'm like, we've been together for quite a while. Let's just commemorate this thing man, baby.”

a4502.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4502.name: Donald Trump
a4502.title: US President
a4502.speech: Promised Tuesday that he is just getting started, touting the "most successful first 100 days of any administration in the history of our country" ; told reporters he was on track to accomplish all of his second-term goals: "I think either we've done everything, or it's in the process of being done," Trump said before heading to his rally ; Trump said he missed the campaign trail.

a4502.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4502.name: Donald Trump
a4502.title: US President
a4502.speech: Listing targets of his ire, said Joe Biden is "sleepy," the media is "fake," judges who oppose him are "communist," Democratic opponents are "radical left," and friendly countries have "abused us more so than foe on trade"; the president promised to conclude deals on trade, but provided little in the way of details.

a4502.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4502.name: Donald Trump
a4502.title: US President
a4502.speech: Criticized Federal Reserve chairman Jerome Powell Tuesday as "not really doing a good job."

a4502.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4502.name: Donald Trump
a4502.title: US President
a4502.speech: Claimed the pledge to end the Ukraine war within 24 hours was made "in jest."

a4502.speaker: Jerome Powell, Federal Reserve chairman
a4502.name: Jerome Powell
a4502.title: Federal Reserve chairman
a4502.speech: Has warned that Trump's tariffs would likely reignite inflation.

a4502.speaker: Donna Fitzsimons, 65-year-old merchandise seller at the Michigan rally venue
a4502.name: Donna Fitzsimons
a4502.title: 65-year-old merchandise seller at the Michigan rally venue
a4502.speech: "He's amazing. Everybody's worried about tariffs. We don't care — look at everything else that's coming together too" ; "People don't realize it takes time to get where you need to go."

a4502.speaker: Democratic National Committee
a4502.name: Democratic National Committee
a4502.speech: "Trump is to blame for the fact that life is more expensive, it's harder to retire, and a 'Trump recession' is at our doorstep," the Democratic National Committee said, calling the 100 days a "colossal failure."

a4502.speaker: CNN
a4502.name: CNN
a4502.speech: Reported that he made the 24-hour Ukraine pledge more than 50 times before taking office, and was even at pains to point out that he was being serious.

a4603.speaker: Omar Sarjo, 40-year-old former corporal in the Gambian military
a4603.name: Omar Sarjo
a4603.title: 40-year-old former corporal in the Gambian military
a4603.speech: “I cultivate cassava…and bananas, and other crops. That is what is helping me. The difficulty there is, as a family man, you can't just sit. My wife helps too.”

a4603.speaker: Omar Sarjo, 40-year-old former corporal in the Gambian military
a4603.name: Omar Sarjo
a4603.title: 40-year-old former corporal in the Gambian military
a4603.speech: “I felt so bad. It is an allegation that destroyed my life.” ; “You know who Salifu Sarjo is. If you're accused of being his son, people would assume you will be like him. People discriminate against me everywhere.” ; “… As soon as they see the name Omar Sarjo from Kabakel, they remember I'm the one accused of being Salifu Sadio's son.”

a4603.speaker: Omar Sarjo, 40-year-old former corporal in the Gambian military
a4603.name: Omar Sarjo
a4603.title: 40-year-old former corporal in the Gambian military
a4603.speech: “… I could have used that D180,000 on something else. I have a piece of land. I could have fenced it and built it little by little.” ; “…It is difficult, really. Being a man who is not working but needs to feed a family, and the children need to go to school too. It is hard.” ; “… I really face huge difficulties – huge ones. And the Army— an institution I served for 13— is responsible.” ; confirmed that until the beginning of October he had not met with the Ministry or the army.

a4603.speaker: Alagie Saidy Barrow, former captain in the US military and director of research and investigation at the Truth Commission
a4603.name: Alagie Saidy Barrow
a4603.title: former captain in the US military and director of research and investigation at the Truth Commission
a4603.speech: Said what happened to Omar is an indictment of the army's recruitment process; said the military recruitment process should have provided safeguards which make it impossible for someone to get through with fake documents. “Who was at the door when he (Omar) came in? What happened to that person? We don't know, and that is just as important to know.”

a4603.speaker: Gambian military (investigation report)
a4603.name: Gambian military (investigation report)
a4603.speech: The military claimed it conducted an investigation— on a tip-off supplied by an unnamed informant— which confirmed that Omar was Salif Sadio's son; the report, which the military claimed was classified, was presented before the court but never made public. Three years later, the army conducted another investigation, confirming their initial story was untrue; another allegation then emerged that he went into the army using someone's document.

a4603.speaker: Magistrate Court in Banjul (ruling)
a4603.name: Magistrate Court in Banjul (ruling)
a4603.speech: Acquitted and discharged Omar Sarjo on charges of attempting to acquire a Gambian passport illegally.

a4603.speaker: High Court of The Gambia (November 2021 judgment)
a4603.name: High Court of The Gambia (November 2021 judgment)
a4603.speech: Sided with Omar, declaring that the army acted wrongly in dismissing him.

a4603.speaker: Sering Momodou Njie, Gambian Minister of Defence
a4603.name: Sering Momodou Njie
a4603.title: Gambian Minister of Defence
a4603.speech: Told lawmakers on 10 July 2024 that they were yet to hear from the justice ministry; in another appearance before parliament on September 18, 2024, told lawmakers of their intent to meet Omar during the week.

a4603.speaker: Ministry of Justice of The Gambia (legal advice to the Ministry of Defence)
a4603.name: Ministry of Justice of The Gambia (legal advice to the Ministry of Defence)
a4603.speech: Claimed the judgment that established the illegality of the army's decision to sack Omar fell short of asking for his reinstatement: “…Mr Omar Sarjo cannot be reinstated into the Gambia Armed Forces because the judgement is not executory.”

a4603.speaker: Lamin J Darboe, constitutional lawyer
a4603.name: Lamin J Darboe
a4603.title: constitutional lawyer
a4603.speech: Does not think the Ministry of Defence requires legal advice to act on Omar's case; likened the case to that of Ya Kumba Jaiteh, where the Supreme Court held that the President's decision to sack her as a nominated lawmaker was unconstitutional. “The declarations in both cases are self-executory and the public bodies concerned must simply rectify their erroneous decisions. Mr. Sarjo was at no point dismissed and he is owed all his entitlements and must be reinstated.”

a4603.speaker: Sering Momodou Njie, Minister of Defence, and Rohey Bittaye, permanent secretary (non-response)
a4603.name: Sering Momodou Njie
a4603.title: Minister of Defence, and Rohey Bittaye, permanent secretary (non-response)
a4603.speech: Reached out to for comment about their intended meeting with Omar, but no comment could be obtained until the time of publication.

a4603.speaker: Col. Lamin K. Sanyang, spokesperson of the Gambia Armed Forces (non-response)
a4603.name: Col. Lamin K. Sanyang
a4603.title: spokesperson of the Gambia Armed Forces (non-response)
a4603.speech: Questions were sent but no reply was received until publication.

a4771.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a4771.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a4771.title: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a4771.speech: Warned about what he considered obstacles to business, alluding to the US administration's decisions to raise tariffs and extend travel bans to a further 36 African countries, including the Portuguese-speaking states Angola, Cape Verde and São Tomé and Príncipe: “When 36 countries in Africa do not have, or are denied, visas to the United States, how can trade develop between the two areas? When tariffs are imposed abusively against African states, and in some cases more than 40%, how is business going to develop?” ; “We are developing policies to mobilise national resources, but we cannot accept the refusal of visas. We cannot accept unfortunate tariffs that have nothing to do with the rules of the World Trade Organisation.”

a4771.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a4771.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a4771.title: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a4771.speech: Lamented that AGOA (the African Growth and Opportunity Act) had been ended, as well as USAID's development aid programmes: “All of that was abandoned. Someone was saying that this is a wake-up call for African nations,” stressing that Africa will increasingly depend on its own domestic resources.

a4771.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a4771.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a4771.title: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a4771.speech: Stressed that the new African Union Commission has focused on the challenges of peace and integration to pacify the continent and promote key sectors such as minerals and energy, health and agro-industry, infrastructure and the digital economy, “bearers of development and prosperity” ; “There is no doubt that Africa has natural and human resources, 30% of the world's mineral resources are on the continent, with a population of 1.4 billion inhabitants.”

a4771.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a4771.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a4771.title: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a4771.speech: Described the US as “a financial and knowledge hub”, stressing the importance of a balanced, fair and equitable partnership so that AU member states open their markets and attract capital, recalling that in 2025 average growth in Africa is estimated at 3.9% and more than 21 countries will have growth above 5% ; “In addition, the fight against corruption and the progressive lifting of tariff and non-tariff barriers is the objective pursued by our member states,” underlining that the continent is firmly engaged in harmonising trade, domestic and financial policies ; highlighted the private sector as one of the main drivers of development, with “the combination of public policies and the private sector” guaranteeing a better future for African nations, and said it is important to introduce reforms to the global financial system and the rules of the World Trade Organisation.

a4771.speaker: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a4771.name: Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
a4771.title: Chairperson of the African Union Commission
a4771.speech: Said that the next G20 Summit in South Africa “will be a good opportunity for Africa's voice to be heard, loud and clear”, underlining that the African continent is considered by many to be the power centre of future global growth.

a4820.speaker: Study by economist Robin Sherbourne on Namibia-EU trade and investment
a4820.name: Study by economist Robin Sherbourne on Namibia-EU trade and investment
a4820.speech: The findings highlight the growing importance of the EU as Namibia’s largest export market, particularly in sectors like agriculture, fisheries, and minerals; the study also outlines the key sectors that have seen significant investment from the EU, including mining, renewable energy, infrastructure, manufacturing and green hydrogen.

a4820.speaker: Ana Beatriz Martins, EU ambassador to Namibia
a4820.name: Ana Beatriz Martins
a4820.title: EU ambassador to Namibia
a4820.speech: emphasised the significance of the economic partnership agreement (EPA) between the EU and Namibia, which has granted Namibia duty-free and quota-free access to the EU market since 2004 ; “This will help us better understand the evolution of Namibia’s exports to Europe, trends by destination, sectors and investments” ; further highlighted that such data strengthens policy analysis, identifies growth opportunities and supports economic planning ; “It can also underpin more efficient resource allocation, for instance, identifying where investment in infrastructure, such as ports and logistics, is most needed. This is particularly important within the context of the EPA and the strategic partnership on raw materials value chains and renewable hydrogen between the EU and Namibia.”

a4820.speaker: European Union
a4820.name: European Union
a4820.speech: revealed that the private sector in Europe has shown a strong commitment to Namibia’s economic diversification, particularly in the transition to green energy and industrialisation.

a4820.speaker: Ana Beatriz Martins, EU ambassador to Namibia
a4820.name: Ana Beatriz Martins
a4820.title: EU ambassador to Namibia
a4820.speech: “Trade is not just about exchanging goods; it is an instrument for development. Our partnership with Namibia is about fostering long-term sustainable growth, creating jobs and building a resilient economy for the future.” ; noted that future collaboration would focus on improving critical infrastructure, such as ports and logistics networks, which are key to facilitating trade and attracting further investment ; announced that the EU and Namibia are working together as part of the Global Gateway initiative, which aims to support the development of green technologies and renewable energy across the continent ; “The EU is not just a trading partner; it is a strategic ally in Namibia’s journey towards prosperity and sustainability.”

a4878.speaker: African News (cited report)
a4878.name: African News (cited report)
a4878.speech: According to African News, the South African government is still involved in a tax dispute, involving the ruling party, the African National Congress (ANC), and the Democratic Alliance (DA).

a4878.speaker: Government of South Africa
a4878.name: Government of South Africa
a4878.speech: Stated that a 0.5% increase in VAT will help the country to offset its budget deficit of 13.5 billion.

a4878.speaker: Democratic Alliance (DA)
a4878.name: Democratic Alliance (DA)
a4878.speech: Said that it could not support a tax increase that would place a further burden on the poor majority of the country's population; the party took the Government to court in an attempt to block the VAT increase from 0.5% to 15.5% as proposed by the Government.

a4878.speaker: Opposition parties and civil society
a4878.name: Opposition parties and civil society
a4878.speech: Criticised the proposed budget as anti-poor.

a4878.speaker: Latest South African budget (document)
a4878.name: Latest South African budget (document)
a4878.speech: According to the latest budget, more than 20 million people in South Africa depend on social grants, with an unemployment rate above 32%.

a4921.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, Dr., President of the African Development Bank Group
a4921.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a4921.title: Dr., President of the African Development Bank Group
a4921.speech: Warned that higher US tariffs could trigger significant economic disruptions across Africa, affecting numerous nations and accelerating a strategic shift in global partnerships ; revealed that 47 of Africa's 54 countries will be impacted directly by the new U.S. trade policies, with potential declines in export revenues and foreign exchange reserves ; “When those currencies weaken, two things will happen: first, you will find that most of these countries are import-dependent. So, you're going to find that high inflation becomes a problem” ; “And secondly, you find that the cost of actually servicing a lot of their debt, which is foreign currency debt but in local currencies, is going to get worse.”

a4921.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, Dr., President of the African Development Bank Group
a4921.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a4921.title: Dr., President of the African Development Bank Group
a4921.speech: Emphasized that Africa cannot afford a trade confrontation with the United States, noting that the continent accounts for only 1.2 percent (approximately $34 billion) of America's global trade—with a trade surplus of just $7.2 billion ; proposed a pragmatic three-point strategy for the continent: engage the U.S. through flexible and constructive trade negotiations, diversify export markets to reduce dependency on any single partner, and accelerate the African Continental Free Trade Area implementation to unlock the potential $3.4 trillion market ; stressed the need to expand Africa's domestic market and boost domestic savings, and that the continent must take advantage of increasing external interest in its natural resources, such as cobalt and lithium, to negotiate a better trade and investment deal ; dismissed any notion of binary alignment: “U.S is a key ally of Africa—and so is China. Africa is building bridges, not isolating itself” ; “I think at the end of the day, we want to make sure that whatever deals that are being done with Africa are transparent, fair, equitable, and led by Africa and in Africa's interests.”

a4921.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, Dr., President of the African Development Bank Group
a4921.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a4921.title: Dr., President of the African Development Bank Group
a4921.speech: Firmly rejected the long-standing paradigm of foreign aid dependency: “The era of aid as we've known it is completely gone,” he declared, calling instead for bold investments in domestic resource mobilization, infrastructure, and value-added industrialization ; said aid must be turned into concessional financing to allow multilateral financial institutions like the African Development Bank to do more for the continent by mobilizing more private capital to develop and derisk projects ; cited the impact of the African Development Fund: “Every dollar (of the African Development Fund) leverages $10, and that's the way to put in money—that's the way to have sustainable impact” ; cited the great potential of Mission 300: “Because without electricity, what can you do? You can't industrialize, you can't add value, and you can't be competitive in the dark” ; highlighted the achievements of the Africa Investment Forum, saying it has mobilized more than $225 billion in investment interest ; believes Africa is the largest greenfield investment destination in the world and remains “the investor's dream”: “We got hydropower. We have a massive youth population that can become the labor force of the world. Sixty-five percent of the arable land left in the world to feed almost 9.5 billion people by 2050 is in Africa, so what Africa does with it will determine the future of food in the world.”

a4921.speaker: African Development Bank Group (statement)
a4921.name: African Development Bank Group (statement)
a4921.speech: A statement from the Bank said Dr. Akinwumi Adesina was interviewed with CNN's Christiane Amanpour.

a5185.speaker: Evariste Ndayishimiye, President of the Republic of Burundi
a5185.name: Evariste Ndayishimiye
a5185.title: President of the Republic of Burundi
a5185.speech: Called on the Burundian authorities to be advocates of good governance, because it is the path toward the eradication of every kind of division and discrimination in the country ; in his opening remarks urged them to be advocates of good governance, stressing that it is essential for each and every person to understand that God alone is the source of power, and called on the country's senior officials to be good leaders for everyone by keeping away from all injustice, jealousy and hypocrisy, because such practices are contrary to good governance ; reminded Burundians to promote unity, mutual assistance and collective work because together everything is possible, and called on everyone to put an end to the struggles in the race for power, recalling that God alone chooses the servants of the people.

a5185.speaker: Evariste Ndayishimiye, President of the Republic of Burundi
a5185.name: Evariste Ndayishimiye
a5185.title: President of the Republic of Burundi
a5185.speech: Urged Burundians to develop still further a patriotic spirit with the aim of moving toward emergence in 2040 and development in 2060 ; reassured participants and Burundians in general that the future is promising, calling on everyone to equip themselves with a vision of the future in order to achieve the development so much desired in the country, to overcome fear and to make their own the vision of Burundi as an emerging country in 2040 and a developed one in 2060, and urged them not to despair because the country's future is in God's hands.

a5185.speaker: Gelase Daniel Ndabirabe, President of the National Assembly of Burundi
a5185.name: Gelase Daniel Ndabirabe
a5185.title: President of the National Assembly of Burundi
a5185.speech: In his welcome address, went back over the history of the National Prayer Breakfast, initiated in the United States of America in 1953 for the American elite.

a5205.speaker: Marius Kudumo, public policy analyst
a5205.name: Marius Kudumo
a5205.title: public policy analyst
a5205.speech: Says the motion calling for the lifting of the U.S. blockade on Cuba is crucial against the backdrop of the current geopolitical situation in the world, and is one of the most important motions recently tabled in Parliament, adding that it is grounded in strong principles and values: “And these values are contained in the Namibian constitution. It is about the values of the inherent dignity of every person, democracy, the rule of law and justice for all. If there is injustice in any part of the world on the basis of the principles and values upon which the Namibian state is established.”

a5205.speaker: Marius Kudumo, public policy analyst
a5205.name: Marius Kudumo
a5205.title: public policy analyst
a5205.speech: “I think we are seeing the geopolitical situation in the world moving in the direction that we do not want to see.” ; “If you look at the establishment of international organisations like the United Nations, they are there to maintain peace and to avoid us repeating the mistakes of the past. Because of these geopolitical issues and the unresolved issues of the Cuba blockade, which is actually coming from the Cold War, I think it is important to remind ourselves that there are still people in the world who are suffering economically, socially, and politically.”

a5205.speaker: Marius Kudumo, public policy analyst
a5205.name: Marius Kudumo
a5205.title: public policy analyst
a5205.speech: Stated that he does not think this motion could impact Namibia's diplomatic relations with the United States, especially given its cooperation through programmes like PEPFAR, and added that Namibia and the US have mutual interests in collaborating with each other: “I don't think it has any implications on bilateral relations, but of course, international relations are fluid, dynamic and unpredictable. Therefore, we cannot state with authority that there are no implications.”

a5205.speaker: Tobie Aupindi, Swapo MP
a5205.name: Tobie Aupindi
a5205.title: Swapo MP
a5205.speech: Tabled a motion calling for the lifting of the U.S. blockade on Cuba, debate on which is set to resume in the National Assembly.

a5355.speaker: Prosecutors (in the Sean Kingston fraud case)
a5355.name: Prosecutors (in the Sean Kingston fraud case)
a5355.speech: Allege that the two, after defrauding various traders by failing to make payment for the goods, still went on using those goods.

a5355.speaker: Magistrate/judge in the case (court ruling)
a5355.name: Magistrate/judge in the case (court ruling)
a5355.speech: Ruled that Kingston's mother should remain in custody after she was found to be a flight risk, while Kingston was given release pending their sentencing on July 11, 2025.

a5363.speaker: Bonifatius Wakudumo, Kavango East Governor
a5363.name: Bonifatius Wakudumo
a5363.title: Kavango East Governor
a5363.speech: Criticized the organisers of the ‘Men Commitment Walk’ for failing to mobilise attendance. "I leave my title as governor, representing the president, and get in my own car, not the government's. I have to arrange for people to gather here, and without my efforts, this event would have flopped." ; "You who are running these events come here and stand around; you don't mobilise people. What do you do? You just wait for attendees? How are people supposed to come to the meeting? I had to send my grandson in my own car to get this podium. This is in Rundu. Are we sabotaging this government, or what is happening? I have to be frank: we cannot work like this, colleagues."

a5373.speaker: Gideon Saar, Israel's Foreign Minister
a5373.name: Gideon Saar
a5373.title: Israel's Foreign Minister
a5373.speech: Fiercely criticised the hearings, calling them part of a "systematic persecution and delegitimisation" of Israel; speaking from Jerusalem, Saar condemned the court as "completely politicised," labelling the process "shameful."

a5373.speaker: U.N. General Assembly (resolution sponsored by Norway)
a5373.name: U.N. General Assembly (resolution sponsored by Norway)
a5373.speech: Asked the ICJ to rule on whether Israel must "ensure and facilitate the unhindered provision of urgently needed supplies essential to the survival of the Palestinian civilian population."

a5373.speaker: World Food Program (as reported by AP)
a5373.name: World Food Program (as reported by AP)
a5373.speech: Announced last week that its food supplies in the Gaza Strip have been exhausted under Israel's nearly eight-week blockade, cutting off a critical source of sustenance for hundreds of thousands of Palestinians.

a5373.speaker: Israeli Foreign Ministry
a5373.name: Israeli Foreign Ministry
a5373.speech: Did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

a5373.speaker: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right allies
a5373.name: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right allies
a5373.speech: Have accused the agency (UNRWA) of being heavily infiltrated by Hamas.

a5373.speaker: UNRWA
a5373.name: UNRWA
a5373.speech: Firmly denies the claim that it is heavily infiltrated by Hamas.

a5373.speaker: Israel (government allegations)
a5373.name: Israel (government allegations)
a5373.speech: Alleges that 19 of UNRWA's roughly 13,000 staff members in Gaza participated in Hamas' October 7, 2023, attack on southern Israel; later alleged that around 100 other Palestinians employed by UNRWA were Hamas members, but it has not provided evidence to the UN.

a5373.speaker: Israel (government allegations)
a5373.name: Israel (government allegations)
a5373.speech: Has also accused Hamas of using U.N. facilities for military purposes, including building tunnels near U.N. buildings and diverting humanitarian aid.

a5373.speaker: South Africa
a5373.name: South Africa
a5373.speech: In a separate case last year, accused Israel of committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza; on Tuesday, South Africa — a vocal critic of Israel — will present its arguments.

a5373.speaker: Israel
a5373.name: Israel
a5373.speech: Strongly denies the charge of committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza.

a5643.speaker: Shashwat Saraf, country director of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a5643.name: Shashwat Saraf
a5643.title: country director of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a5643.speech: Warns, “The situation in Tawila is collapsing” ; describes families sleeping on the bare ground under makeshift shelters, with almost no access to drinking water or toilets, while cholera cases rise.

a5643.speaker: Shashwat Saraf, country director of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a5643.name: Shashwat Saraf
a5643.title: country director of the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a5643.speech: Warns, “The window to save thousands of lives is closing rapidly” ; calls for immediate and unhindered international support to deliver humanitarian aid to Tawila before the situation becomes uncontrollable.

a5643.speaker: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) assessment, June, in the camps
a5643.name: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) assessment
a5643.title: June, in the camps
a5643.speech: Reveals alarming conditions among the 213,000 people living there: only 10% have access to a reliable water source, fewer than 10% have latrines, and the majority of families eat only one meal a day; about 39% of women are pregnant or breastfeeding, 22% of households include people with disabilities who receive no care, and thousands of children are deprived of school.

a5643.speaker: Joint assessment by local authorities and humanitarian organisations (Al Fasher)
a5643.name: Joint assessment by local authorities and humanitarian organisations (Al Fasher)
a5643.speech: Indicates that 38% of children under five suffer from acute malnutrition, 11% of them in a critical state.

a5691.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a5691.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a5691.speech: Has raised concerns over escalating health emergencies across multiple regions, warning that millions remain at risk due to funding shortages and ongoing conflicts.

a5691.speaker: Hanan Balkhy, WHO Regional Director for the Eastern Mediterranean
a5691.name: Hanan Balkhy
a5691.title: WHO Regional Director for the Eastern Mediterranean
a5691.speech: Speaking at a press briefing on Tuesday, said the situation has been further complicated by the United States' recent decision to halt its financial contributions to the organisation; described the withdrawal as a major setback, highlighting the agency's longstanding reliance on US contributions for critical health interventions: “The regrettable US announcement to withdraw will have an enormous impact on the WHO and the wider humanitarian sector” ; explained that the Stop Work Order has already disrupted operations, particularly in emergency response efforts.

a5691.speaker: Hanan Balkhy, WHO Regional Director for the Eastern Mediterranean
a5691.name: Hanan Balkhy
a5691.title: WHO Regional Director for the Eastern Mediterranean
a5691.speech: Highlighted that the United States has historically been WHO's largest contributor, providing 18 per cent of its 2024/25 biennial budget, along with significant voluntary funding for key programmes like polio eradication and disease surveillance in conflict zones; noted that this heavy reliance on a single donor was unsustainable: “We have long known that we must diversify our sources of funding” ; urged more countries, particularly those in the Eastern Mediterranean region, to increase their contributions to safeguard vulnerable populations and strengthen global health security.

a5691.speaker: Hanan Balkhy, WHO Regional Director for the Eastern Mediterranean
a5691.name: Hanan Balkhy
a5691.title: WHO Regional Director for the Eastern Mediterranean
a5691.speech: Reiterated calls for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza, sustained humanitarian assistance, and the restoration of basic services.

a5691.speaker: Hanan Balkhy, WHO Regional Director for the Eastern Mediterranean
a5691.name: Hanan Balkhy
a5691.title: WHO Regional Director for the Eastern Mediterranean
a5691.speech: Said the organisation is responding to 16 graded emergencies, including seven complex humanitarian crises and over 50 disease outbreaks, with six emergencies reaching the highest crisis level ; “In Sudan, 20 million people need urgent health assistance, and some 25 million will experience acute food insecurity by June this year. Yet, the health cluster response is only 5.6 per cent funded” ; “In Syria, 65 per cent of the population need emergency health assistance, at a time when 70 per cent of the health workforce has left the country, and fewer than half of the nation's hospitals still function.
