But WHO faces a funding shortfall of more than 80 per cent” ; said funding shortages in Afghanistan could force the closure of 80 per cent of WHO-supported essential healthcare services by June this year and negatively impact gains made over decades in the fight against polio; added that WHO's ability to manage cholera outbreaks in Yemen, provide trauma care in Gaza, and combat malnutrition in Sudan is at risk.

a5691.speaker: Hanan Balkhy, WHO Regional Director for the Eastern Mediterranean
a5691.name: Hanan Balkhy
a5691.title: WHO Regional Director for the Eastern Mediterranean
a5691.speech: Revealed that Member States have agreed in principle to a 20 per cent increase in assessed contributions for the 2026–27 budget, pending approval at the World Health Assembly in May; stressed that sustainable and diversified funding is critical: “In our own Region, there are nations increasingly making their mark in the humanitarian arena. We urge them to turn their attention to health. Their moment is now.”

a5691.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (executive order)
a5691.name: Donald Trump
a5691.title: US President (executive order)
a5691.speech: In January, shortly after his inauguration, signed an executive order withdrawing the country from WHO, citing political influence within the agency.

a5721.speaker: Bill Gates, billionaire and Microsoft co-founder
a5721.name: Bill Gates
a5721.title: billionaire and Microsoft co-founder
a5721.speech: Pledged on Thursday to donate almost his entire fortune by 2045, aiming to give away around 200 billion dollars to the world's poor via his foundation; announced that he would speed up his wealth donation process on the 25th anniversary of the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, and said the foundation will close once it has spent 99% of his fortune.

a5721.speaker: Bill Gates, billionaire and Microsoft co-founder
a5721.name: Bill Gates
a5721.title: billionaire and Microsoft co-founder
a5721.speech: In February 2025, pointed out that his Foundation could not work miracles, but that "we'll be showing that we're doing the most we can": "The need of course, is far greater than what we can do. But we'll be showing that we're doing the most we can and give a lot of predictability to the field. By having this, we'll be here all of those 20 years but not thereafter."

a5721.speaker: Forbes Billionaires List
a5721.name: Forbes Billionaires List
a5721.speech: Named Gates richest man on earth for several consecutive years until 2018; he is today the 13th richest person, with a fortune estimated at 108 billion dollars.

a5758.speaker: Bloomberg
a5758.name: Bloomberg
a5758.speech: Reported that the bridge funding, running from October through March, is part of the State Department’s America First Global Health Strategy, which prioritises the procurement and distribution of goods from U.S. companies and seeks to reduce dependency on long-term aid

a5758.speaker: U.S. PEPFAR bridge funding package (recommendations)
a5758.name: U.S. PEPFAR bridge funding package (recommendations)
a5758.speech: Includes recommendations to prioritise frontline health workers and essential medical supplies; however, some services, such as male circumcision, abortion, and related communication campaigns, will not be covered

a5758.speaker: Mathematical modelling study published in eClinicalMedicine
a5758.name: Mathematical modelling study published in eClinicalMedicine
a5758.speech: Shows the transformative impact of PEPFAR in expanding access to antiretroviral therapy (ART) across sub-Saharan Africa: the number of people on ART has risen from almost zero in the early 2000s to about 21 million by 2023, HIV/AIDS-related deaths fell from 2.2 million in 2003 to 390,000, and new infections declined from 3.2 million to 640,000 over the same period

a5819.speaker: Livestock and Livestock Products Board of Namibia (latest trade statistics)
a5819.name: Livestock and Livestock Products Board of Namibia (latest trade statistics)
a5819.speech: According to the latest trade statistics from the Livestock and Livestock Products Board of Namibia, cattle exports declined from the 45 597 cattle marketed in April last year to 13 196 herds of cattle marketed in April 2025; on a year-on-year basis live exports in the last two months stood at 74.83%, lower than observed in April 2024; weaner auction prices increased by N$7.58/kg from N$24.83/kg in April 2024 to N$32.41/kg in April 2025; total sheep marketing declined by 47.72%, from 116 879 sheep marketed in April last year to 61 104 in April this year, with live exports down 39.09% and export abattoir performance down 45.84% year-on-year, while slaughtering at B and C class abattoirs decreased by 83.40% from 21 038 sheep in April 2024 to 3 493 in April this year.

a5819.speaker: Fransina Angula, trade and strategic marketing statistician at the Livestock and Livestock Products Board of Namibia
a5819.name: Fransina Angula
a5819.title: trade and strategic marketing statistician at the Livestock and Livestock Products Board of Namibia
a5819.speech: Said despite being only five months into the new year, the enduring effects of the drought remain evident ; "The livestock sector has been severely impacted, leaving it with limited market-ready animals to supply across various marketing channels. This has led to contractions across all sectors, with the exception of the pig sector, which recorded growth during February 2025. Livestock prices on the other hand soared as limited supply of animals drove up shortages. The drought of 2024 posed immense challenges for farmers, necessitating increased cattle marketing as a response to the harsh environmental conditions. Consequently, farmers experienced significant herd reductions, leaving them with minimal market-ready livestock during the current year," observed Angula ; "The livestock and livestock products’ sector in general posted a negative performance in terms of output which saw producer prices rising. The current trend is mainly driven by a shortage of animals after drought, while the advent of good rainfalls support efforts to rebuild stocks."

a5948.speaker: Minister of Energy of Mali
a5948.name: Minister of Energy of Mali
a5948.speech: Speaking to the press last week, assured that a plan is in place to minimise cuts in the coming days; without going into details, he promises significant efforts to ensure a better service.

a5948.speaker: Director General of Energie du Mali (EDM-SA)
a5948.name: Director General of Energie du Mali (EDM-SA)
a5948.speech: Also gave reassurance that all arrangements have been made to ensure the success of Mali's load-shedding programme, called “Plan Unique”, which provides for coverage of 80% of Malians' energy needs per day, that is, 19 hours of electricity per day out of 24.

a6005.speaker: Janine Walz, Head of Cooperation at SECO and Deputy Head of Mission
a6005.name: Janine Walz
a6005.title: Head of Cooperation at SECO and Deputy Head of Mission
a6005.speech: Praised Ghana's government for "walking the talk" in rallying diverse stakeholders behind meaningful policy dialogue; noted that the new NDPS provides Development Partners (DPs) and international NGOs an opportunity to shape Ghana's next phase of decentralisation reforms ; "The policy being developed presently offers all DPs and INGOs the chance to shape this successor policy," she said, urging continued collaboration to achieve a consensus-driven, reform-oriented, and practical framework for local governance.

a6005.speaker: Dr. Gameli Kewuribe Hoedoafia, Executive Secretary of the Inter-Ministerial Coordinating Committee on Decentralisation (IMCC)
a6005.name: Dr. Gameli Kewuribe Hoedoafia
a6005.title: Executive Secretary of the Inter-Ministerial Coordinating Committee on Decentralisation (IMCC)
a6005.speech: Highlighted that the draft policy had undergone extensive consultations nationwide, gathering input from four zonal sub-national meetings and a national stakeholder forum with Ministries, Departments, and Agencies, and CSOs; underscored the importance of DP feedback to align with the aspirations and to finalise the policy that truly reflects local needs.

a6278.speaker: Statement of Financial Position of the Bank of Tanzania for August 2025
a6278.name: Statement of Financial Position of the Bank of Tanzania for August 2025
a6278.speech: Shows that the Bank has strengthened its gold reserves, reaching gold worth 821.8 billion shillings as of August 31, 2025.

a6278.speaker: Bank of Tanzania, July 2025 Monetary Policy Report
a6278.name: Bank of Tanzania
a6278.title: July 2025 Monetary Policy Report
a6278.speech: Explained that gold purchases were aimed at strengthening the shilling amid global challenges ; “The escalating geopolitical tensions, trade frictions, and changes in U.S. foreign aid policies added to global uncertainty, prompting banks to rebalance their portfolios and manage risk exposure” ; “Domestic gold purchases by the Bank have increased liquidity, which has partly reduced pressure on the shilling.”

a6278.speaker: World Gold Council
a6278.name: World Gold Council
a6278.speech: According to the World Gold Council, in June the leading gold purchasers included: Uzbekistan (9 tons), Kazakhstan (7 tons), Singapore (6 tons), and China, Turkey, and the Czech Republic (2 tons each); in Africa, Ghana led with 1 ton; in July, Kazakhstan again led with 3 tons, while Turkey, China, and the Czech Republic each bought 2 tons.

a6278.speaker: Uganda
a6278.name: Uganda
a6278.speech: Announced it had begun holding gold reserves.

a6278.speaker: Russia
a6278.name: Russia
a6278.speech: Insisted it had no intention of invading Poland.

a6278.speaker: Poland
a6278.name: Poland
a6278.speech: Has strongly rejected Russia’s claim, maintaining that Russia has hostile plans against it.

a6337.speaker: Global Bar Magazine (report)
a6337.name: Global Bar Magazine (report)
a6337.speech: According to Global Bar Magazine, the Somali government has expelled Anna Saleem Högberg, Sweden's consul and head of development cooperation in Mogadishu, amid growing diplomatic tensions. ; Sources cited by Global Bar Magazine indicated that Somali authorities accused Högberg of damaging the government's image—an allegation that played a key role in the decision to expel her.

a6337.speaker: Somali officials
a6337.name: Somali officials
a6337.speech: Somali officials have not issued a formal statement.

a6337.speaker: Multiple sources familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a6337.name: Multiple sources familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a6337.speech: Say the expulsion followed a rift between Högberg and the office of Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre; the disagreement reportedly escalated over several months before culminating in her removal in March.

a6337.speaker: Officials from Sweden's Foreign Ministry and the development agency Sida
a6337.name: Officials from Sweden's Foreign Ministry and the development agency Sida
a6337.speech: Declined to comment on the matter.

a6447.speaker: Benin Demographic and Health Survey, 5th edition (EDSB-5) report
a6447.name: Benin Demographic and Health Survey
a6447.title: 5th edition (EDSB-5) report
a6447.speech: Reports that more than four out of five women who had a live birth in the past 5 years (83%) received antenatal care from a qualified provider; that on average 78% of births took place with the assistance of qualified personnel and 84% in a health facility; that 86% of children under 5 had their birth registered with the civil registry; that one child in 3 (33%) aged 5-17 worked above the threshold defined for his or her age group; and that the majority of children (91%) aged 1-14 underwent some form of violent discipline. The survey, run from 6 November 2017 to 28 February 2018, sampled 14,435 households with a 99% response rate.

a6447.speaker: Laurent Hounsa, Director General of the National Institute of Statistics and Economic Analysis (INSAE)
a6447.name: Laurent Hounsa
a6447.title: Director General of the National Institute of Statistics and Economic Analysis (INSAE)
a6447.speech: Said the EDSB is an operational survey carried out every five years since 1996, and that the results of the EDSB-5 allow policymakers and partners to better choose development policies; he thanked all those who contributed to carrying out the survey.

a6447.speaker: Allan Read, USAID Resident Representative in Benin and lead of the technical and financial partners
a6447.name: Allan Read
a6447.title: USAID Resident Representative in Benin and lead of the technical and financial partners
a6447.speech: Considers that the data collected are essential for decision-making at all levels — decisions which, he adds, are for the planning and design, for the next five years, of development policies.

a6447.speaker: Abdoulaye Bio Tchane, Minister of State for Planning and Development of Benin
a6447.name: Abdoulaye Bio Tchane
a6447.title: Minister of State for Planning and Development of Benin
a6447.speech: Declared that he was moved by a sentiment resting on two essential reasons: first, that this dissemination phase comes at a time when the government has undertaken an overhaul of the national statistical system to make it more efficient and productive — “This will enable us to meet the requirements of national and international agendas such as the Government Action Programme (PAG), the National Development Programme (PND), the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the African Union's Agenda 2063”; and second, that it concerns a crucial subject touching on the well-being of the population in general and social protection in particular. He further notes that the SDGs refer to it, through SDG 3, which aims to “Give individuals the means to live a healthy life and promote the well-being of all at all ages”.

a6650.speaker: Mark Steyn, Canadian newspaper columnist, author of America Alone: The End of the World as We Know It
a6650.name: Mark Steyn
a6650.title: Canadian newspaper columnist, author of America Alone: The End of the World as We Know It
a6650.speech: Thought demographic shifts, cultural decline, and Islam would ruin Western civilisation, and that the only redeeming grace was American exceptionalism; his book title extolled America as the last bastion of civilisation as we know it.

a6650.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6650.name: Donald Trump
a6650.title: US President
a6650.speech: Accused Mexico and Canada of not doing enough to control the flow of fentanyl, a potent synthetic opioid analgesic more than 50 times more powerful than morphine, into the US ; apart from his perennial accusations against China of stealing US technology and other unfair trade practices, also accused Beijing of sending ingredients for making fentanyl to Mexico.

a6650.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (second inaugural address)
a6650.name: Donald Trump
a6650.title: US President (second inaugural address)
a6650.speech: Said that his "proudest legacy will be that of a peacemaker and unifier."

a6650.speaker: Adam Smith, economist
a6650.name: Adam Smith
a6650.title: economist
a6650.speech: Once described a trade war as "beggar-thy-neighbour."

a6650.speaker: Analysts
a6650.name: Analysts
a6650.speech: Before the one-month tariff pause between the US and its neighbours, forecast the tariffs would hinder US GDP growth by approximately 0.25 per cent to 0.3 per cent, that the tariffs on Canada and Mexico alone could decrease overall economic output by around $45 billion, with potential losses escalating to $75 billion following retaliatory measures.

a6698.speaker: Ministry of Health of Uganda
a6698.name: Ministry of Health of Uganda
a6698.speech: Is optimistic that Uganda will get the second consignment of COVID-19 vaccines on time despite the shortages experienced globally.

a6698.speaker: Government of Uganda
a6698.name: Government of Uganda
a6698.speech: Had initially said that the doses would cover 482,000 people, with each getting two injections spaced between eight weeks, before the plan was later revised to allow more people to get the first dose.

a6698.speaker: Serum Institute of India
a6698.name: Serum Institute of India
a6698.speech: Announced the halting of vaccine exports to first serve their domestic market; said its production capacity was very stressed, and feared that it could not have the capacity to meet the production targets given its agreement to supply 166 million doses to the Indian government.

a6698.speaker: Jane Ruth Aceng, Minister of Health of Uganda
a6698.name: Jane Ruth Aceng
a6698.title: Minister of Health of Uganda
a6698.speech: Says that there is no need to worry because President Yoweri Museveni and the country is looking for an opportunity to get the vaccine here in time ; says that there is hope that the COVAX facility will give Uganda vaccines in early May for both those who got the vaccine and those who didn't.

a6698.speaker: COVAX facility
a6698.name: COVAX facility
a6698.speech: Committed to providing Uganda with over three million doses of the AstraZeneca vaccine in the first half of 2021.

a6698.speaker: Several MPs (Ugandan Members of Parliament)
a6698.name: Several MPs (Ugandan Members of Parliament)
a6698.speech: Had raised concerns about the second dose of vaccine, saying Uganda had not yet secured the vaccines yet a first-round was almost getting complete.

a6698.speaker: Jane Ruth Aceng, Minister of Health of Uganda
a6698.name: Jane Ruth Aceng
a6698.title: Minister of Health of Uganda
a6698.speech: Said that there is no health risk if one doesn't get a second dose of vaccine.

a6755.speaker: National Anti-Corruption Forum (statement issued by Cosatu general secretary Zwelinzima Vavi on behalf of 39 civil society formations)
a6755.name: National Anti-Corruption Forum (statement issued by Cosatu general secretary Zwelinzima Vavi on behalf of 39 civil society formations)
a6755.speech: Announcing a mass mobilisation against corruption and abuse of power, declared that "corruption is the biggest threat to our young democracy" and that the forum will be developing a "concrete detailed platform" to mobilise civil society: "We have agreed to coordinate our activities within and between all civil society formations to ensure that these anti-corruption campaigns have a maximum impact on corruption. We shall use the forum as a loose campaign structure to conduct a campaign that will expose corruption without fear or favour, irrespective of the individuals and institutions concerned. Key to the campaign will be to ensure that information is disseminated in a manner that empowers grassroots structures and a bottom-up approach in future campaigns." It went on to say that information will be shared among all participating civil society formations through a website/email network and social media.

a6755.speaker: National Anti-Corruption Forum (statement)
a6755.name: National Anti-Corruption Forum (statement)
a6755.speech: On its demands: "We call for new laws to be introduced that will not allow families of the political leadership, including trade unions and civil society, from doing business with government. We call for new laws that will ensure that we deal with the phenomenon of javelin throwing and specifically call for all senior civil servants and political leaders not be allowed to do business with the state after they have left the public service for a period of between two to five years." The forum also called for lifestyle audits to be periodically conducted on all political leaders, senior public servants, and civil society and trade union leaders.

a6755.speaker: Zwelinzima Vavi, Cosatu general secretary
a6755.name: Zwelinzima Vavi
a6755.title: Cosatu general secretary
a6755.speech: On his internal Cosatu opponents, speaking at metalworkers union Numsa's national bargaining conference, lashed out at those leading the onslaught against him, saying he was now of the view that "there will be no common ground with those leaders, whoever they may be", and claiming that those leaking damaging allegations about him to the media were at the level of presidents and general secretaries of affiliate unions: "They have been given a mandate to destroy Cosatu or at best create so much division that the federation can no longer be an independent movement capable of fighting for the interests of members. The mandate of the sources is very clear: target the general secretary and smear him continuously in the newspapers until workers lose trust in him... Either they succeed to divide and weaken Cosatu, or we expose them and crush them. The real reason why they won't disclose their identities is that they act without any mandate from the members of their unions. Eventually we shall defeat these few individuals acting as sources of the newspapers; we have no doubt about that."

a6755.speaker: Zwelinzima Vavi, Cosatu general secretary
a6755.name: Zwelinzima Vavi
a6755.title: Cosatu general secretary
a6755.speech: On Cosatu's economic demands: said Cosatu had submitted a Section 77 notice at the National Economic Development and Labour Council - "Our demands, amongst many others, are state intervention in strategic sectors of the economy, including through nationalisation, addressing the unemployment crisis through creation of decent work, promoting active industrialisation, eradication of poverty, a 40-hour working week, banning of labour broking and access to free quality education and healthcare."

a6755.speaker: Zwelinzima Vavi, Cosatu general secretary
a6755.name: Zwelinzima Vavi
a6755.title: Cosatu general secretary
a6755.speech: On the National Development Plan: "The NDP's economic and labour market proposals constitute a serious assault on workers. Cosatu will not support them." ; "It is simply unfair for anyone, in particular our ally the ANC, to ask us to cooperate with our own oppression and exploitation, which is what the NDP's major proposals are. The NDP represents a typical example of the chicken and a pig partnership in which the chicken offers to lay eggs for breakfast but asks the pig to donate bacon."

a6755.speaker: Zwelinzima Vavi, Cosatu general secretary
a6755.name: Zwelinzima Vavi
a6755.title: Cosatu general secretary
a6755.speech: On campaigning on social issues, including e-tolling: called for motorists to defy e-tolling and said at the Numsa conference, "We will never apologise for campaigning on social issues outside the workplace, which directly affect the quality of life of the workers and their families."

a6755.speaker: Union leaders from the National Union of Mineworkers and the National Education Health and Allied Workers Union
a6755.name: Union leaders from the National Union of Mineworkers and the National Education Health and Allied Workers Union
a6755.speech: Believe that Vavi is straying from Cosatu's agreed positions when he attacks the ANC and government, and is therefore effectively locating Cosatu as a formation in the opposition to the ANC.

a6840.speaker: Senaykrem Mekonnen, General Manager of Ethio Robotics
a6840.name: Senaykrem Mekonnen
a6840.title: General Manager of Ethio Robotics
a6840.speech: Said the aim of the robotics competition is to support students in technology and that it helps them improve their designing, engineering and programming skills, and that beyond that it was prepared with the intention of enabling students to build capacity that will make Ethiopia's name known when they compete on the international stage ; “At the international robotics competition held recently in China, they showed their coding success,” explaining that the competition focuses on coding and helps students understand that they are coders ; said a total of 350 primary, secondary and higher education students took part and that the number of competitors fell below what had been expected because, for various reasons, some did not come from the regional cities ; said the students who win the competition will represent Ethiopia at the international robotics competition to be held in the United States in Ginbot 2017 (May 2025).

a6840.speaker: Selamyihun Adefris, Innovation Development Lead Executive at the Ethiopian Ministry of Innovation and Technology
a6840.name: Selamyihun Adefris
a6840.title: Innovation Development Lead Executive at the Ethiopian Ministry of Innovation and Technology
a6840.speech: Explained that the institution is working so that students' technological knowledge is raised and their creative skills grow, and that a Science, Technology and Innovation Policy has been prepared to help with this and will enable young people to be successful in the technology sector ; “The institution provides support to competitions and activities carried out by various private institutions and academies that encourage science and technology innovations,” indicating that there would be assistance on matters of ideas, funding and technical issues ; explained that although the competition is mostly organised by the private sector, the government carries out monitoring and oversight work so that there are no matters raising questions about the competition and so that it is conducted transparently.

a6840.speaker: Amen Tewodros, ninth-grade student at Kidi Academy and competitor
a6840.name: Amen Tewodros
a6840.title: ninth-grade student at Kidi Academy and competitor
a6840.speech: Said he was able to take part in the competition because he has the ability to do coding and to assemble mechanical things ; “We competed as a team of 13 and were able to win. I am happy about this,” explaining that at the international robotics competition to be held in the United States they will bring innovations that will make Ethiopia's name known ; said he has a dream of becoming a doctor by being successful in his studies, and that his foremost desire is to establish his own hospital and help citizens who suffer from a lack of medical care.

a6889.speaker: Olusegun Obasanjo, former President of Nigeria
a6889.name: Olusegun Obasanjo
a6889.title: former President of Nigeria
a6889.speech: Has faulted African leaders for their thirst and hunger for development aid from the West, speaking during a panel session at the Afreximbank Annual Meeting: “We have lived too long on aid. Is aid the way that Africa should be expecting? I don’t believe so. Now, if that is the case, what should we substitute for aid? We run to Japan. We run to China. And all the African leaders run to China. For how much? China will give up to $20bn… which a country in Africa can produce… and more.” Has also repeatedly described ‘democracy’ as un-African and advocated for what he described as Communalism that prioritises argument and concession instead of opposition politics, which breeds ‘winner-takes-all’ syndrome and bottomless corruption.

a6889.speaker: Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
a6889.name: Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
a6889.speech: According to ECOWAS, an estimated $88.6 billion is illegally moved across borders, often through criminal activities, corruption, and trade misinvoicing.

a6889.speaker: The World Bank
a6889.name: The World Bank
a6889.speech: Has admitted that the IFFs reduce domestic resources and tax revenue needed to fund poverty-reducing programmes and infrastructure in developing countries.

a6893.speaker: Abdulkadir Isse, journalist reporting from the Somali court
a6893.name: Abdulkadir Isse
a6893.title: journalist reporting from the Somali court
a6893.speech: In a revelation first exposed by him, Yahye is the younger brother of Hawo Ahmed Mohamud, Al-Adaala’s mother, making them extremely close family members.

a6893.speaker: Sources at Somalia’s Military Court (anonymous)
a6893.name: Sources at Somalia’s Military Court (anonymous)
a6893.speech: Have revealed that Yahye and Al-Adaala are maternal relatives who grew up in the same household.

a6893.speaker: Defectors from Al-Shabaab who surrendered to Somali authorities
a6893.name: Defectors from Al-Shabaab who surrendered to Somali authorities
a6893.speech: Exposed this connection, revealing that Yahye regularly visited Al-Adaala’s residence in Mogadishu, spending weekends there undetected.

a6893.speaker: Horn Observer
a6893.name: Horn Observer
a6893.speech: Reported that Yahye regularly visited Al-Adaala’s residence in Mogadishu, spending weekends there undetected.

a6893.speaker: BBC (reporting)
a6893.name: BBC (reporting)
a6893.speech: As per BBC reporting, the SYL Hotel attack killed eight people, including three Somali soldiers, and injured 27 others, among them three members of parliament and the Somali government spokesperson.

a6893.speaker: Reuters, citing Somalia’s Health Minister, Dr. Ali Haji Adam
a6893.name: Reuters
a6893.title: citing Somalia’s Health Minister, Dr. Ali Haji Adam
a6893.speech: The 10-hour siege at the Lido Beach Hotel resulted in 37 civilian deaths and 247 injuries including two journalists.

a6893.speaker: Somali authorities, through the Military Court
a6893.name: Somali authorities
a6893.title: through the Military Court
a6893.speech: Have now confirmed that Yahye was the mastermind behind both attacks as part of his new role overseeing suicide operations in Mogadishu’s Banadir region.

a6893.speaker: TRAC Terrorism, a research and analysis consortium that tracks over 4,000 terrorist groups
a6893.name: TRAC Terrorism
a6893.title: a research and analysis consortium that tracks over 4,000 terrorist groups
a6893.speech: Recently uncovered that Yahye and Al-Adaala are linked through various business ventures spanning Somalia, Kenya, and Dubai, including powdered milk imports into Mogadishu, allegedly marketed through Banadir Hospital with the involvement of Al-Adaala’s wife, Fartun Sharif; luxury apartments in Nairobi’s Pangani suburb, financed partly by Premier Bank, a Mogadishu-based financial institution accused of laundering funds for Al-Shabaab; and sports equipment stores and real estate projects in Mogadishu, funded by money funnelled through corrupt government contacts.

a6893.speaker: U.S. Treasury Department
a6893.name: U.S. Treasury Department
a6893.speech: In January 2025 sanctioned Yemen Kuwait Bank, citing its financial dealings with Premier Bank, which has been suspected of facilitating terrorist transactions including the Houthi militia group in Yemen.

a6893.speaker: Kenya’s National Terrorism Financing Risk Assessment Report (December 2023)
a6893.name: Kenya’s National Terrorism Financing Risk Assessment Report (December 2023)
a6893.speech: According to the report, Somalia poses the highest terrorism financing risk to Kenya ; the report warns that large sums of money collected by Al-Shabaab are being laundered into Kenya’s real estate sector, making Nairobi a prime destination for illicit funds.

a6893.speaker: Diplomatic sources (anonymous)
a6893.name: Diplomatic sources (anonymous)
a6893.speech: Reported in April 2024 that Somalia accounts for $180 million and $21.9 million in annual remittances to Kenya and Uganda, respectively.

a6893.speaker: Abdirahman Abdishakur Warsame, Somali MP
a6893.name: Abdirahman Abdishakur Warsame
a6893.title: Somali MP
a6893.speech: Has also raised concerns over stolen Somali government funds being laundered in Kenya.

a6893.speaker: Abdulkadir Nur, anti-money laundering expert
a6893.name: Abdulkadir Nur
a6893.title: anti-money laundering expert
a6893.speech: “Due to its proximity to Somalia and its progressive economy in East Africa, Kenya is seen as an attractive location for criminal and terror networks” ; “While Kenyan authorities are trying their best, the existing regulations remain weak, making it difficult to detect terrorist financing from Somalia.”

a6893.speaker: Intelligence reports
a6893.name: Intelligence reports
a6893.speech: Indicate that both ISIS and Al-Shabaab have increasingly turned to legitimate businesses to sustain their funding, using import/export companies to funnel illicit funds, real estate agents to launder money through property investments, and exploiting Kenyan banks due to weak regulations that fail to detect these financial crimes.

a6893.speaker: Security analysts / Kenyan security experts
a6893.name: Security analysts / Kenyan security experts
a6893.speech: Are urging authorities to take urgent countermeasures, including stronger scrutiny of foreign investments ; Kenyan security experts warn that Nairobi’s real estate sector is being exploited by terror financiers.

a6893.speaker: Some US officials (anonymous, speaking to the Washington Post)
a6893.name: Some US officials (anonymous
a6893.title: speaking to the Washington Post)
a6893.speech: Revealed to the Washington Post their plight as nearly all functions of the Anti-Terrorism Assistance program have been suspended.

a6911.speaker: Constant Lonkeng, IMF Mission Chief for Benin, and Modeste Some, IMF Resident Representative in Benin
a6911.name: Constant Lonkeng
a6911.title: IMF Mission Chief for Benin, and Modeste Some, IMF Resident Representative in Benin
a6911.speech: Presented the progress made under the ongoing programmes and the outlook, and said this decision allows the immediate disbursement of about 80 million US dollars granted directly to the State budget, bringing IMF disbursements to date for the benefit of Benin to more than 600 million dollars ; said the programmes to be financed are designed to support the reforms undertaken in Benin, particularly on debt sustainability and climate action.

a6911.speaker: IMF Executive Board
a6911.name: IMF Executive Board
a6911.speech: Welcomed the very solid performance achieved by Benin, with very strong resilience and growth beyond the expectations formulated at the time of the previous review, driven by exports from the Special Economic Zone.

a6911.speaker: Constant Lonkeng, IMF Mission Chief for Benin, and Modeste Some, IMF Resident Representative in Benin
a6911.name: Constant Lonkeng
a6911.title: IMF Mission Chief for Benin, and Modeste Some, IMF Resident Representative in Benin
a6911.speech: Welcomed climate actions that have won the support of Benin's partners, who at the recent COP29 committed to providing financing in support of the country's climate action ; expressed the wish that the reform be maintained, with the assurance that the living conditions of the population will improve.

a6929.speaker: Ulisses Correia e Silva, Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a6929.name: Ulisses Correia e Silva
a6929.title: Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a6929.speech: Explained in presenting the 2025 State Budget (OE2025): "A budget that stimulates and encourages economic growth and employment" ; "It ensures macroeconomic stability, with less inflation, with a reduction of the debt burden, and it sets priorities: development of human capital, strengthening and consolidation of connectivity, strengthening the promotion of inclusion, accelerating the diversification of the economy, accelerating the energy, climate and digital transition. It strengthens investment, acting on transformational factors to increase the competitiveness and productivity of the economy, the efficiency and quality of public administration, and the economic, social and environmental resilience of the country."

a6929.speaker: Ulisses Correia e Silva, Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a6929.name: Ulisses Correia e Silva
a6929.title: Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a6929.speech: Said of policy consistency: "Economic and social reality is only transformed in the long term, on the basis of a shared vision, perseverance and sustainability" ; "A good budget is one that is consistent. Sometimes people say there is nothing new, or that we are keeping the policies; if we discontinue the policies, we lose consistency."

a6929.speaker: Olavo Correia, Minister of Finance of Cabo Verde
a6929.name: Olavo Correia
a6929.title: Minister of Finance of Cabo Verde
a6929.speech: Said at the public session presenting the OE2025: "This is a budget whose bottom line is to produce an impact" ; "And the main impact is the creation of qualified jobs and embracing our strategy of promoting social inclusion by way of employment and income" ; "And for that to happen, we need to invest a lot. Invest on the public-sector side, which is very important so that we can facilitate private investment, and create conditions for the private sector to invest in Cabo Verde - national private investors, our diaspora, but also foreign private investors."

a6929.speaker: Olavo Correia, Minister of Finance of Cabo Verde
a6929.name: Olavo Correia
a6929.title: Minister of Finance of Cabo Verde
a6929.speech: Added, on the international context: "If in the international context we have uncertainties, unpredictability, insecurity, the only way for us to respond is by promoting stability, confidence and predictability in Cabo Verde."

a6929.speaker: 2025 State Budget guidelines (OE2025 document)
a6929.name: 2025 State Budget guidelines (OE2025 document)
a6929.speech: Sets out 23 priorities, including strengthening governmental efficiency, consolidating internal and international connectivity, combating extreme poverty, resolving outstanding professional matters in the public administration, deepening investment in business development, energising economic activities in rural areas, delivering priority public infrastructure, accelerating the energy transition, boosting the diversification of the economy and increasing the potential for economic growth; according to the document, the reform of social protection and the extension of the contributory regime to hard-to-cover groups will contribute to reducing inequalities in access to health and will strengthen income protection for people in situations of unemployment; and according to the OE2025 the MCC compact should act as an accelerator with regard to connectivity and mobility in their land, air, maritime, technological and human dimensions and within the framework of intermodality.

a6983.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a6983.name: Wang Yi
a6983.title: Chinese Foreign Minister
a6983.speech: Says China's cooperation with Africa continues to yield visible and tangible results: "China remains one of Africa's largest trade partners for over sixteen years. My African brothers and sister, China Africa Corporation is visible, tangible and truly a vision" ; "In the past three years alone, Chinese enterprises created more than 1.1 million new jobs in Africa."

a6983.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a6983.name: Wang Yi
a6983.title: Chinese Foreign Minister
a6983.speech: Argued that the China-Africa cooperation is a strategic partnership that is built on the aspiration of transforming livelihood, advancing industrialization and agricultural modernization ; explained that China-Africa cooperation aimed at raising Africa's voice and representation at the international level, adding that China's foreign policy stands firmly on international justice and opposes power politics and hegemony ; stated that China's foreign policy also focuses on advancing a cooperation with a shared future inherited in people-centered governance and advancement of the livelihood of people.

a6983.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a6983.name: Wang Yi
a6983.title: Chinese Foreign Minister
a6983.speech: Said Africa is experiencing a new awakening, and countries should support it in exploring this new development.

a6983.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a6983.name: Wang Yi
a6983.title: Chinese Foreign Minister
a6983.speech: Disclosed that this year marks the beginning of implementing the outcome of the Forum on China Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) Beijing Summit: "Also, this year marks the 20th anniversary of FOCAC. Over the past twenty-five years, China has helped Africa build nearly one hundred kilometers of roads and more than ten thousand kilometers of railways" ; "China stands ready to deliver on the ten partnership action that China and Africa seek to jointly advance modernization, including supporting Africa in accelerating its industrialization, agriculture modernization, implementing zero tariff treatment for 100% tariff free, fostering new sanitary life with new growth to harvest like digital green, and AI industry and promoting one thousand small and beautiful projects, enhancing governance experience sharing and rising representation on voice of Africa in international office."

a6983.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a6983.name: Wang Yi
a6983.title: Chinese Foreign Minister
a6983.speech: Stated that this year the D20 summit will be held on the African continent for the first time, adding that the summit supports Africa in carrying out its duties as G20 President and in leading a proper African mark in global governance.

a6983.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a6983.name: Wang Yi
a6983.title: Chinese Foreign Minister
a6983.speech: Described China and Africa as good friends, saying they are brothers that shared a single future, and noted that under the guidance of China President Xi Jinping and African leaders, the China Africa relationship is now at its best in history ; said China has established strategic partnerships with all African countries that have diplomatic ties with it, and the China Africa Community with the Shared Future has been elevated ; indicated that Africa is a third tier of the twenty-first century and there will be no global modernization without Africa's modernization, asserting that the stability of development is quite in true humanity and the world must listen to Africa and heed its concerns.

a6987.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6987.name: Donald Trump
a6987.title: US President
a6987.speech: Has long been keen to defend workers from the “carnage” of “bad trade deals” ; also threatened the European Union (EU) with trade barriers on automobiles and could take even more measures on intellectual property rights and technology goods.

a6987.speaker: European Union
a6987.name: European Union
a6987.speech: Warned the United States not to take such measures.

a6987.speaker: EU Trade Ministers
a6987.name: EU Trade Ministers
a6987.speech: Agreed at a meeting on 27 February 2018 that they would respond with counter-measures if the United States brings in import tariffs on steel and aluminum.

a6987.speaker: Matthias Machning, German Deputy Economy Minister
a6987.name: Matthias Machning
a6987.title: German Deputy Economy Minister
a6987.speech: Stated that the introduction of tariffs on steel and aluminum by the United States is incompatible with the World Trade Organization (WTO) rules and unjustifiable on national security grounds.

a6987.speaker: Ralph Ossa, University of Chicago
a6987.name: Ralph Ossa
a6987.title: University of Chicago
a6987.speech: Recent estimations indicate that a global trade war, resulting in a rise in trade barriers for all countries, would slash real incomes by an average 3.4%; at the global level, this would correspond to a loss of almost one full year of growth efforts ; argued that President Trump's such move is surprising in that it will negatively impact the United States economy, although the extent of harm would be limited to the loss of jobs in the user industries of the protected sector ; said this can be illustrated with the case of the United States steel safeguard tariffs between March 2002 and December 2003, when President George W. Bush imposed safeguard tariffs ranging between 8% and 30% on ten steel product groups, with exemptions for NAFTA countries, other preferential trade agreement parties and 100 developing countries.

a6987.speaker: Ralph Ossa, University of Chicago
a6987.name: Ralph Ossa
a6987.title: University of Chicago
a6987.speech: Said the lack of an investment treaty between the United States and China adds considerable fuel to the flames; if such an investment treaty existed, it would assure fair access to reciprocal markets for multinationals.

a6987.speaker: Dr. Agnieszka Gehringer, Senior Research Analyst, Flossbach von Storch Research Institute
a6987.name: Dr. Agnieszka Gehringer
a6987.title: Senior Research Analyst, Flossbach von Storch Research Institute
a6987.speech: Stated that, as a result of trade restrictions, United States imports of steel products declined by 5% between 2002 and 2003, bringing the steel industry's trade deficit down by 28%; however, immediately after the protection ended, import growth rebounded and contributed to a rapid widening of the industry's trade deficit, above the levels from the pre-protectionist era.

a6987.speaker: Dr. Agnieszka Gehringer, Senior Research Analyst, Flossbach von Storch Research Institute
a6987.name: Dr. Agnieszka Gehringer
a6987.title: Senior Research Analyst, Flossbach von Storch Research Institute
a6987.speech: Said nine WTO members (Brazil, China, Chinese Taipei, the EU, Japan, Korea, New Zealand, Norway and Switzerland) opposed the safeguard measures in the WTO; it was found that the safeguards violated WTO rules by failing to show a “causal link” between increased imports and “serious injury” on the United States side, and that the United States government did not provide comprehensive and appropriate evidence of “unforeseen developments” of steel imports explaining their increase.

a6987.speaker: Dr. Agnieszka Gehringer, Senior Research Analyst, Flossbach von Storch Research Institute
a6987.name: Dr. Agnieszka Gehringer
a6987.title: Senior Research Analyst, Flossbach von Storch Research Institute
a6987.speech: Further noted that there should be no doubt that unfair trading practices undermine the harmonious functioning of the global trading order, but the WTO's dispute resolution has exactly the aim to assist discordant trading partners in a peaceful resolution of trade tensions; the United States enjoys an above-average success rate in disputes decided at the WTO since its foundation in 1995, while some WTO rules might be indeed outdated and could be renegotiated to better reflect the changing nature of trade today.

a6987.speaker: Steve Halle, Birmingham University
a6987.name: Steve Halle
a6987.title: Birmingham University
a6987.speech: Stated that the current Trump administration's strategy reflects a false diagnosis of the underlying problem of chronic current account deficits registered by the United States; as long as United States excess consumption is financed by savings from abroad, there is no economic reason for current account deficits to improve, and protectionism only reallocates the deficits among sectors ; noted that under the twin deficit scenario, these trade deficits could get even worse, should the recent major tax cuts significantly worsen the outlook for the United States fiscal balance.

a6987.speaker: Thomas Jefferson, former US President (quoted)
a6987.name: Thomas Jefferson
a6987.title: former US President (quoted)
a6987.speech: “The most successful war seldom pays for its losses.”

a7065.speaker: Many experts
a7065.name: Many experts
a7065.speech: Warn that diseases will surge [following U.S. President Trump's spending freeze on foreign aid].

a7065.speaker: Research for the Copenhagen Consensus think-tank
a7065.name: Research for the Copenhagen Consensus think-tank
a7065.speech: Shows that additional expenditure of $6.2 billion annually could save about a million lives a year over coming decades, making this one of the very best possible development policies; this spending would enable a much broader diagnosis to end onwards infections and ensure most tuberculosis patients stay on medication, reducing deaths by 90 per cent by 2030, with benefits outweighing the health care and time costs by 46 to 1.

a7166.speaker: Boston Maliketi Banda, Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM) spokesperson
a7166.name: Boston Maliketi Banda
a7166.title: Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM) spokesperson
a7166.speech: Said the bank’s measures are designed to move Malawi away from seasonal forex dependence to a more durable foundation. ; “We are also formalising mineral revenue streams and linking financial institutions with the private sector to finance export-oriented production. These policies are meant to sustain a stable exchange rate and gradually strengthen our import cover,” Banda said.

a7166.speaker: RBM data
a7166.name: RBM data
a7166.speech: Show Malawi recorded a cumulative trade deficit of $1.6 billion (K1.7 trillion) between January and June 2025, up 15 percent from the same period last year.

a7166.speaker: Economists
a7166.name: Economists
a7166.speech: Caution that once tobacco sales end, the deficit could widen again.

a7166.speaker: Velli Nyirongo, Scotland-based economist
a7166.name: Velli Nyirongo
a7166.title: Scotland-based economist
a7166.speech: “This is temporary relief,” warned Scotland-based economist Velli Nyirongo. “Without structural reforms and export diversification, Malawi risks sliding back.”

a7166.speaker: Government of Malawi
a7166.name: Government of Malawi
a7166.speech: Says efforts are underway to address this.

a7166.speaker: Patrick Botha, Ministry of Trade and Industry spokesperson
a7166.name: Patrick Botha
a7166.title: Ministry of Trade and Industry spokesperson
a7166.speech: Said the National Export Strategy II prioritises crops such as macadamia, legumes, maize seed, coffee, tea, and sugar, as well as tourism and transport services.

a7175.speaker: Mozambican government
a7175.name: Mozambican government
a7175.speech: Said today that at least 2,500 jobs have been lost in Mozambique due to the cut in US foreign aid through the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), admitting that this poses “a problem” to the economy.

a7175.speaker: Ivete Alane, Mozambican Minister of Labour, Gender and Social Action
a7175.name: Ivete Alane
a7175.title: Mozambican Minister of Labour, Gender and Social Action
a7175.speech: “The last meeting I had with the group set up by organizations that work, that benefited from the funding, they talked of around 2,500 [jobs], but that was the information that was given, that I have to this day and I believe that it must be more or less that,” said the Minister in Maputo on the sidelines of the 2nd Conference on Social Services, while admitting that there was no “official estimate” ; “We are always aware of work, there are jobs that are being lost, jobs are being lost, this is a problem and we expect the economy to flourish so that we can produce more jobs.”

a7175.speaker: Lusa (data released)
a7175.name: Lusa (data released)
a7175.speech: According to data released by Lusa on February 4, 2025, Mozambique was the member of the Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP) that received the most USAID funding in 2023, totalling US$664.122 million; in the CPLP universe, Angola followed Mozambique on the list of largest recipients of USAID aid in fiscal year 2023, with US$71.320 million, joined, in descending order, by Brazil with US$68.985 million and Timor-Leste with US$43.688 million.

a7262.speaker: Simon Lionel Loyara, head of advertising at the communications agency Interactive, representing the Gilda brand
a7262.name: Simon Lionel Loyara
a7262.title: head of advertising at the communications agency Interactive, representing the Gilda brand
a7262.speech: “We have come to respond to the call for contributions from the President of Faso, Captain Ibrahim Traore, who, through this fund, calls on us to come and contribute in order to support and help our defence and security forces who are engaged in the theatre of operations,” declared Loyara, who underlined Gilda's long-standing commitment in Burkina Faso ; “We made this donation to complete a collective action that we have just carried out, that is to say that we made a first donation at the level of the patriotic support fund. We wrote a cheque, we gave a cheque of 3 million there, and we are completing it with a donation of food supplies for displaced persons” ; “The message is really that everyone should lend a hand for the building of our very dear homeland.”

a7262.speaker: Ibrahim Traore, Captain, President of Faso
a7262.name: Ibrahim Traore
a7262.title: Captain, President of Faso
a7262.speech: Called on citizens to contribute to the Patriotic Support Fund (FSP) in order to support and help the defence and security forces engaged in the fight against terrorism.

a7262.speaker: Vieux Abdoul Rachid Soulama, secretary general of the Ministry of Economy and Finance
a7262.name: Vieux Abdoul Rachid Soulama
a7262.title: secretary general of the Ministry of Economy and Finance
a7262.speech: Welcomed the contribution: “Much more than a financial contribution, your gesture rings out as the expression of the support and recognition shown towards the fighting forces for the efforts made day and night on the battlefields in order to preserve the honour and the dignity of our people” ; underlined the importance of the collective mobilisation that makes it possible to provide monthly support for more than 65,000 combatants, equipped and provided with improved hygiene conditions, thanks to various contributions, in order to preserve the integrity of the country.

a7262.speaker: Sibila Ouedraogo, head of the solidarity and humanitarian action service, Provincial Directorate of Humanitarian Action of Kadiogo
a7262.name: Sibila Ouedraogo
a7262.title: head of the solidarity and humanitarian action service, Provincial Directorate of Humanitarian Action of Kadiogo
a7262.speech: Said the donation will contribute to improving the daily ration of the beneficiaries and to relieving their suffering. “I would like to express aloud our gratitude to Gilda, which has brought a very much appreciated donation to vulnerable people” ; specified that the hierarchy will put in place a targeting process to identify the beneficiaries according to defined criteria.

a7410.speaker: Maureen Malavé, USAID/Ghana Nutrition and Social Protection Lead
a7410.name: Maureen Malavé
a7410.title: USAID/Ghana Nutrition and Social Protection Lead
a7410.speech: “This is an important step in ensuring that communities not only have access to nutritious food but also good health and social services,” said during the grant announcement in Tamale.

a7453.speaker: Doctors and programme managers
a7453.name: Doctors and programme managers
a7453.speech: Say that after the US announced a permanent end to funding for HIV projects, services across the board have been affected, from projects helping orphans and pregnant women to those reaching transgender individuals and sex workers.

a7453.speaker: Modelling (HIV mortality projections for South Africa)
a7453.name: Modelling (HIV mortality projections for South Africa)
a7453.speech: Suggests the cuts could result in 500,000 deaths over the next 10 years in South Africa.

a7453.speaker: US government
a7453.name: US government
a7453.speech: Has announced it will be cutting more than 90% of the contracts of its key development agency, USAid, and slashing $60bn (£48bn) of overseas aid spending.

a7453.speaker: The Guardian
a7453.name: The Guardian
a7453.speech: Has heard that notices of termination have been sent to organisations in other countries in the region, including Malawi, Zambia, Tanzania and Zimbabwe, as well as with the joint United Nations programme UNAids.

a7453.speaker: Elizabeth Glaser Paediatric Aids Foundation
a7453.name: Elizabeth Glaser Paediatric Aids Foundation
a7453.speech: Said it had received termination notices for three of its projects, which provide HIV treatment for more than 350,000 people in Lesotho, Eswatini and Tanzania, including more than 10,000 HIV-positive pregnant women.

a7453.speaker: Dr Lynne Mofenson, senior adviser at the Elizabeth Glaser Paediatric Aids Foundation
a7453.name: Dr Lynne Mofenson
a7453.title: senior adviser at the Elizabeth Glaser Paediatric Aids Foundation
a7453.speech: Said the decision was "a death sentence for mothers and children".

a7453.speaker: Trump administration
a7453.name: Trump administration
a7453.speech: Announced a 90-day review of foreign aid in late January, forcing many projects to stop work.

a7453.speaker: Prof Linda-Gail Bekker, director of the Desmond Tutu HIV Centre at the University of Cape Town
a7453.name: Prof Linda-Gail Bekker
a7453.title: director of the Desmond Tutu HIV Centre at the University of Cape Town
a7453.speech: "It is not hyperbole to say that I predict a huge disaster" ; her modelling suggests a complete loss of Pepfar funding in South Africa would lead to more than 500,000 extra HIV deaths over a decade ; said it was likely things would go backwards ; said she had initially expected the US to target programmes working with key groups such as the LGBT+ community, because of the Trump administration's attacks on diversity initiatives, "but in fact, this has been across the board. This is children, this is orphans, vulnerable children, young women and girl programmes. It is generic and across the board" ; said it also halts ongoing research, including trials into potential HIV vaccines and new prevention drugs ; said US funding had allowed projects to fill gaps in government provision, such as clinics where transgender people or sex workers can seek care without stigma or legal concerns.

a7453.speaker: Kholi Buthelezi, national coordinator at Sisonke, a sex workers' organisation
a7453.name: Kholi Buthelezi
a7453.title: national coordinator at Sisonke, a sex workers' organisation
a7453.speech: "I've been having sleepless nights. This blow, it reminded us of back when there was no cure for HIV." ; at a press briefing on the cuts, she and others working on HIV in South Africa called on their government to "step up" and fill the gaps left by the US's withdrawal.

a7453.speaker: Dr Kate Rees, public health medicine specialist at the Anova Health Institute
a7453.name: Dr Kate Rees
a7453.title: public health medicine specialist at the Anova Health Institute
a7453.speech: Said programmes with funding from the CDC have not yet been forced to shut, but said it was too early to conclude that those programmes were safe ; said there had already been plans to shift programmes reliant on donors to government funding over the next five years, but "now, instead of a careful handover, we're being pushed over a cliff edge" ; said US funding had been embedded in the health system and so the withdrawal would "be felt by everyone who uses or works in health services" ; "Tomorrow we are letting go more than 2,800 people. That's counsellors, data capturers, healthcare workers - and these people are not going to find other jobs very easily."

a7487.speaker: Elon Musk, billionaire entrepreneur (social media post)
a7487.name: Elon Musk
a7487.title: billionaire entrepreneur (social media post)
a7487.speech: Claimed on social media that the organisation is “literally state-funded media”; his remark followed his reposting of a claim suggesting that the United States government funds the BBC through its international development agency, USAID.

a7487.speaker: BBC Media Action (statement)
a7487.name: BBC Media Action (statement)
a7487.speech: Has reiterated its independence from the BBC national broadcaster; the charity responded with a firm statement clarifying its independence from BBC News and the UK government. “BBC Media Action is completely separate from BBC News, and wholly reliant on our donors and supporters to carry out our work.”

a7487.speaker: BBC Media Action (statement)
a7487.name: BBC Media Action (statement)
a7487.speech: Confirmed that former US President Donald Trump’s recent decision to pause all USAID funding had affected its operations. “Like many international development organisations, BBC Media Action has been affected by the temporary pause in US government funding, which amounts to about 8% of our income in 2023-24.” The charity assured stakeholders that efforts were underway to mitigate the effects of the funding suspension: “We’re doing everything we can to minimise the impact on our partners and the people we serve.”

a7487.speaker: BBC Media Action’s accounts
a7487.name: BBC Media Action’s accounts
a7487.speech: According to the accounts, USAID was its second-largest donor in 2023-24, providing £2.61 million, behind the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), which contributed £3.02 million.

a7487.speaker: Several other UK charities, including Stonewall
a7487.name: Several other UK charities
a7487.title: including Stonewall
a7487.speech: Have also reported that the USAID funding pause would negatively affect their operations.
